item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Vibrant Villages Programme
Strengthening India's Frontiers Through Inclusive Development
Posted On: 06 SEP 2026 11:00AM by PIB Delhi

The Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP) has redefined the role of India's border villages. They are no longer remote outposts. They are now strategic partners in national security and development. The programme is implemented through VVP-I and VVP-II, with a combined outlay of Rs 11,639 crore. It is expanding road connectivity, electricity, telecommunications, healthcare, education and livelihood opportunities across villages along India's international land borders. VVP seeks to build vibrant, resilient and prosperous border communities. It improves quality of life and creates sustainable economic opportunities. In doing so, it strengthens India’s border security by sustaining thriving communities along its frontiers.

 

Why the Border Village Matters

India shares over 15,000 kilometres (km) of international land border with seven neighbouring countries. The longest stretch runs 4,096.7 km along the border with Bangladesh. China follows at 3,488 km and Pakistan at 3,323 km. Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan account for the remainder.

For decades, many border villages remained isolated by difficult terrain, weak connectivity, limited infrastructure and few livelihood opportunities. These challenges triggered out-migration, leaving several frontier areas sparsely populated. To address these longstanding issues, the Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP) was launched in 2023. It seeks to accelerate the comprehensive development of selected villages along India's borders. Recognising border residents as the eyes and ears of the border guiding forces, it aims to build vibrant, secure and prosperous frontier communities. The programme also marks a shift in perspective by treating these settlements not as the nation's last villages, but as its first.

Starting with northern border villages, the Government has expanded the programme across the entire land frontier in phases. Empowered border communities form the foundation of a secure and strong Viksit Bharat@2047.

Did You Know? The first warning of the 1999 Kargil intrusion did not come from a radar or a patrol. On 3 May 1999, local residents were the first to report suspicious movement in the Kargil sector. This underscores the importance of border communities as the first line of defence for the nation.

 

Two Phases, One Frontier Mission

The Government is implementing the Vibrant Villages Programme in two phases that together cover India's entire international land border. VVP-I covers villages along the northern border. VVP-II extends the same approach to the other international land borders. Together, the two phases aim to cover more than 2616 villages with a combined outlay of Rs. 11,639 crore.

The two phases differ in design but share a single purpose. VVP-I is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented with the States, while VVP-II is a Central Sector Scheme funded fully by the Centre. Both phases of the initiative aim to improve living conditions, generate local livelihoods and empower border communities. They work to strengthen the nation's border security by developing "first villages" as vibrant centres of growth.

VVP-I: Strengthening Northern Border Communities

The first phase of the VVP was announced in the Union Budget 2022-23 for villages along the northern border. It was launched at Kibithoo in Anjaw district of Arunachal Pradesh on 10 April 2023. The villages in 46 blocks abutting northern border in 4 States and 1 UT in 19 Districts were identified out of which 662 strategic villages were taken on priority for comprehensive development covering a population of about 1.42 lakh. These are Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand and the Union Territory of Ladakh. The scheme was approved with an outlay of Rs 4,800 crore. This covers the financial years 2022-23 to 2026-27. Out of this amount, Rs 2,500 crore was earmarked for road connectivity. The programme aims to bridge the development gap in remote border villages. It strives to provide quality infrastructure and essential services to them comparable to those available elsewhere in the country.

Did You Know? Kibithoo was chosen to launch the VVP due to its strategic location, history and development needs. Located in Arunachal Pradesh's Anjaw district, it is among India's easternmost inhabited villages. The area witnessed fierce fighting during the 1962 India–China War. Remote terrain, sparse connectivity and out-migration have long constrained development. Launching the Programme from Kibithoo reflected the Government's vision of bringing development first to the nation's frontier.

Key interventions under VVP-I

The programme supports all-weather roads, drinking water, reliable electricity, mobile and internet connectivity, and essential healthcare and education infrastructure. It also promotes tourism facilities and multi-purpose community centres to improve livelihoods and the overall quality of life. Livelihood support is organised on a hub-and-spoke model. It encourages social entrepreneurship, the empowerment of youth and women, the promotion of tourism and local culture, and one-block-one-product enterprises. By creating convergence, VVP-I established the delivery model that the second phase now carries to the rest of the land border.

      

Did You Know? India has been supporting border villages for nearly four decades. The Border Area Development Programme (BADP) was launched in 1986-87 along the western border. It was later expanded to cover villages within 10 km from the first habitation from international border. It covered 111 districts across 16 States and 2 Union Territories, and sanctioned over 39,000 development works since 2004-05. The programme is now in its sunset phase. Building on this foundation, VVP focuses on selected border villages. It ensures they receive every applicable government scheme, helping people stay in their villages and strengthen border security.

VVP-II: Extending the Model to All Land Borders

The Union Cabinet approved VVP-II on 2nd April, 2025. Unlike the first phase, VVP-II is funded entirely by the Centre and implemented by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). It was formally launched on 20th February, 2026 at Nathanpur village in Cachar district of Assam. The scheme carries an outlay of Rs. 6,839 crores  till financial year 2028-29.

It has identified 1,954 villages for comprehensive development in 334 blocks abutting the international land borders. These blocks lie in 15 States and 2 Union Territories. The States/UTs are Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tripura, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Jammu and Kashmir (UT) and Ladakh (UT). Blocks on the northern border, already covered under VVP-I have been excluded to avoid duplication of efforts.

Interventions under VVP-II

The Government of India approved a comprehensive package under VVP-II to strengthen border villages. The scheme supports infrastructure, value chains through cooperatives and self-help groups (SHGs), SMART classrooms, tourism circuits and sustainable livelihoods. It also promotes road connectivity, healthcare, financial inclusion, skill development, and telecom connectivity. The objective is to improve living conditions, generate livelihoods and encourage people to stay in border villages. It extends the Vibrant Villages Programme to India's entire land border under a unified development framework.

 

Did You Know?  VVP-II seeks to build prosperous and secure border areas. It places special emphasis on preventing and controlling trans-border crime through stronger border communities.

 

Delivering Development Through Scheme Convergence

The VVP implementation is guided by Village Action Plans. This is to be achieved through border-specific, State-specific and village-specific interventions based on local needs. The programme follows a convergence-based approach, ensuring saturation of schemes under existing norms. All-weather roads are being developed under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)-IV of the Ministry of Rural Development.

Since the border villages face unique challenges, a High-Powered Committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary may recommend relaxations in scheme guidelines to address them. The Ministry of Home Affairs is the nodal ministry. It works closely with State Governments, district administrations and border guarding forces for coordinated planning and implementation.

Impact on the Ground

Since its launch, Vibrant Villages Programme-I has laid the foundation for inclusive and sustainable development in northern border villages.

 

As of July, 2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs has sanctioned 1,248 projects with an outlay of Rs. 3,020.32 crore. A further 1,655 projects have been sanctioned by Central Ministries and Departments under convergence. An amount of Rs. 953.47 crore has been released to the States and the Union Territories, while 283 projects have been reported completed by them. A state/UT wise table for the sanctioned projects is given below.

Connectivity: roads and long span bridges

In all, 111 road projects with an outlay of Rs. 2,481.93 crore have been sanctioned. These roads will connect 134 villages that had no road access earlier. A total of 35 long span bridges were also sanctioned under these projects. Better roads are expected to ease travel, widen local markets and support tourism in these villages.

Tourism as a new source of income

Tourism has become one of the most visible components of the programme on the ground. Under VVP-I, 327 tourism projects with an outlay of Rs. 145 crores have been approved. These include viewpoints, adventure tourism, eco-tourism, eco-resorts, trek routes and tourist centres.

Outreach and service delivery

More than 8,800 activities were held up to 31st July, 2026. These include awareness drives, service delivery camps, health and veterinary camps, and skill training. Arunachal Pradesh recorded 2,990 activities, and Ladakh recorded 2,221 activities. Uttarakhand held 2,038, Himachal Pradesh 1,037 and Sikkim 530 activities.

Did You Know? The Viksit Vibrant Village Programme transforms border villages into living classrooms for India's youth. In 2026, over 400 volunteers from every State and Union Territory spent a week in 74 border villages across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. They engaged in community service, cultural exchange and grassroots development.

VVP: Impact Beyond Infrastructure

The impact of the Vibrant Villages Programme extends beyond infrastructure to strengthen security, livelihoods, governance and community resilience.

Security: A populated and confident border belt supports the work of the border-guarding forces. Both phases seek to create a strong frontier population acting as a strategic asset to the nation.

Demography & Reverse Migration: Livelihood opportunities and improved connectivity give families reason to remain in the border villages. In Arunachal Pradesh, people of border villages of Kurung Kumey, Dibang Valley and Shi-Yomi districts are returning to their villages. This signifies the impact of the programme.

Economy: Border tourism, cooperatives, SHGs and Farmer Producer Organisations are creating a local income base in areas where economic opportunity was previously limited. Local procurement by the border guarding forces adds an assured market within the village itself.

Governance: The saturation approach brings every eligible household in these villages within the reach of existing Central and State schemes. Village Action Plans give the district administration a single instrument for sequencing that work across several departments.

Collectively, these four strands describe a single idea: that development and security are not competing claims on the frontier but reinforce one another.

Did You Know?  In Arunachal Pradesh, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) procures milk, vegetables, eggs and grains directly from vibrant villages. A border post thereby becomes a dependable customer for the farms beside it.

Towards a Connected and Self-Reliant Frontier

The Vibrant Villages Programme is a promise that India's frontier communities will share fully in the nation's progress. Better infrastructure, sustainable livelihoods and convergence of government schemes are creating opportunities closer to home. At the same time, border tourism and local enterprise are unlocking the region's potential. As these villages become more vibrant, prosperous and self-reliant, they will continue to strengthen India's borders and advance the vision of a secure, inclusive and Viksit Bharat by 2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister leads International Vulture Awareness Day 2026 celebrations and inaugurates National Workshop themed ‘From Crisis to Recovery – Conserving India’s Vultures’, at Panchkula
Shri Bhupender Yadav calls for continued creation of Vulture Safe Zones and development of Technical Capacity to aid Species Recovery in the Wild
Posted On: 06 SEP 2026 10:49AM by PIB Delhi


The International Vulture Awareness Day 2026 was celebrated today at Panchkula, Haryana. Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav inaugurated a national-level workshop on the theme ‘From Crisis to Recovery – Conserving India’s Vultures’ on the occasion. The event was also graced by the august presence of Haryana State Minister for Environment, Forest and Wildlife, Shri Rao Narbir Singh, besides senior dignitaries from the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), and Haryana State Government.

The programme was organised in collaboration with the MoEFCC, Central Zoo Authority (CZA), Haryana Forest & Wildlife Department, Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) and the Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre (JCBC), Pinjore. It brought together senior forest officials, scientists, veterinarians, zoo professionals, conservation practitioners and other stakeholders to strengthen collaborative efforts for vulture conservation in India. 

Addressing the gathering, Shri Yadav highlighted that the government's environment conservation approach, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi,  is based on a holistic ecosystem-oriented conservation model and not limited to a particular species. The Minister stated the approach is evident in various species conservation initiatives whether it is Big Cats, Sloth Bear, Great Indian Bustard, Dolphins, Gharial, Wild water buffalo or Vultures. Talking about vultures, he informed how India, which is home to a diverse community resident and migratory vultures - White-rumped, Long-billed, Slender-billed, Red-headed, Egyptian, Himalayan Griffon, Eurasian Griffon, Cinereous and Bearded Vultures - is making efforts towards their successful conservation.

Shri Yadav highlighted the vital ecological role of vultures as highly efficient scavengers and described them as nature’s own cleaning system. By rapidly consuming animal carcasses, vultures facilitate nutrient recycling and help maintain ecological balance. He stated that world is facing challenges like Climate Change, Human-animal conflict and a sharp decline was observed in Indian Vulture population since 1990s mainly due to disruption in their food chain and use of pain killers for animals that were consumed by the vultures. 

The Minister emphasised on coordinated efforts as a 'Whole of Government' and 'Whole of Society' approach in policy making for Vulture conservation. He called for continued efforts to create Vulture Safe Zones through vulture-safe veterinary practices, ensuring safe food availability and technical capacity building to aid species recovery in the wild. The Minister also appealed to veterinary professionals, livestock owners, local administrations and communities to actively contribute to vulture conservation and promote safe carcass-management practices.

Earlier, the Union Minister started the day with a visit to the JCBC Pinjore, where he visited the facility, reviewed a presentation on the Centre and interacted with officials involved in vulture conservation. The Centre, a collaborative initiative of the Haryana Forest Department and BNHS, has emerged as an important centre for conservation breeding of the White-rumped, Long-billed and Slender-billed Vultures. 

It was informed that the Centre undertakes scientific husbandry, artificial incubation, veterinary care, breeding and genetic management. During 2025–26, JCBC housed 356 vultures and successfully bred 35 chicks. It also released or contributed 87 vultures for reintroduction, transferred 90 birds to other conservation-breeding institutions, and trained 1,222 participants from 22 institutions, thereby strengthening technical capacity for vulture conservation.

Addressing the gathering on the occasion, Shri Rao Narbir Singh talked about the important contribution and successful vulture conservation programme being carried out at the Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre (JCBC), Pinjore. He emphasised that the success of conservation breeding should not be measured merely by the number of animals born, but by the establishment of healthy and genetically managed populations, generation of scientific knowledge, development of technical capacity and contribution towards species recovery in the wild. 

During the inaugural session, a Coffee table book - 'Story of Jatayu: Saving India's Vulture' - was released on the occasion. It chronicles India's remarkable vulture conservation story from a declining Vulture population to the successful breeding conservation programme through the establishment of JCBC Pinjore. Further, a prize distribution ceremony was held for the online drawing competition and digital photography competition held on Vulture Conservation. 

The International Vulture Awareness Day 2026 National Workshop was organized with a renewed commitment to ensuring that vultures continue to thrive in India’s landscapes and perform their vital ecological role. The journey ‘From Crisis to Recovery’ reflects India’s collective commitment to vulture conservation through science, policy, conservation breeding, safe landscapes and community participation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Dr. Vinaya Prakash Singh Re-elected APPU Secretary-General for Second Consecutive Term
Posted On: 06 SEP 2026 10:04AM by PIB Delhi

Dr. Vinaya Prakash Singh, a 1988 batch officer of the Indian Postal Service, has been re-elected as Secretary-General of the Asian-Pacific Postal Union (APPU) for a second consecutive four-year term. He was declared elected unopposed by acclamation at the 14th APPU Congress held in Bangkok on September 4, 2026. His re-election reflects the confidence and consensus of postal administrations across the Asia-Pacific region in his leadership and is a significant recognition of India’s contribution to international postal cooperation. His second term will commence in January 2027 and continue until December 2030.

Dr. Vinaya Prakash Singh, Secretary-General, Asian-Pacific Postal Union (APPU)

The re-election comes at a time when the APPU continues to play an important role in strengthening postal cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region. Headquartered in Bangkok, the Union is an intergovernmental organisation comprising 32 member countries and functions as a Regional Union of the Universal Postal Union (UPU), the United Nations specialised agency for the postal sector. Since assuming the position in January 2023 following his first election at the 13th APPU Congress in 2022, Dr. Singh has contributed to advancing cooperation among postal administrations and supporting the development and modernisation of postal services across the region. His second term will provide further opportunity to strengthen regional collaboration and advance shared priorities in the postal sector.

With a career spanning more than three decades, Dr. Singh has held several senior positions in the Government of India, including Member of the Postal Services Board, Senior Deputy Director General and Chief Vigilance Officer in the Department of Posts, Chief Postmaster General, Uttar Pradesh Circle, and Chief General Manager at India Post Headquarters. He has also undertaken assignments with the Union Public Service Commission, the United Nations Development Programme in Afghanistan and the Army Postal Service Corps. An accomplished academic, he was a Gold Medallist in Modern History from the University of Allahabad and holds a Ph.D. in Management from the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi. The Department of Posts congratulates Dr. Vinaya Prakash Singh on his re-election and wishes him a successful and impactful second term as Secretary-General of the Asian-Pacific Postal Union.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Centenary Celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce
Over the years, this institution has given generations of students the opportunity to learn, grow and make a difference: PM
From policy paralysis to policy dynamism, India has come a long way: PM
India's 7.8% growth amid global uncertainty reflects its economic strength: PM
Together, 140 crore Indians will make India both Viksit and Aatmanirbhar: PM
India is moving forward at a new pace; What once took decades is now happening in just a few years: PM
If Indians can lead the world's top companies, Indian companies can lead the world too, It is all possible: PM
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 9:52PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated in centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) today. Addressing the gathering he noted that the occasion is historic for both the college and the nation's education sector as multiple generations have gathered together. “I pay tribute to the founder Shri Ram ji and bow to his vision,” remarked Shri Modi.

Highlighting the profound significance of this 100-year milestone for both the college and the nation's education sector, the Prime Minister paid tribute to founder Shri Ram ji and bowed to his enduring vision. “When an institution turns 100, it becomes an ocean of achievements and inspirations,” observed Shri Modi.

Tracing the college's magnificent evolution from a modest establishment in Daryaganj to a towering educational institution, the Prime Minister noted that it has shaped generations. He acknowledged the immense pride associated with the institution's name today. “Even today in DU, saying you are from SRCC is a flex in itself,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Praising the stellar legacy of the college, the Prime Minister acknowledged the SRCC alumni as original trailblazers who have elevated the institution globally across various fields. He recalled his personal experiences working with notable alumni like the late Arun Jaitley and Sanjeev Sanyal, observing that graduates have excelled as artists, politicians, and judges. “Meaning, the alumni of SRCC have made their mark in every field,” noted Shri Modi.

Reflecting on the widespread nostalgia surrounding the current event, the Prime Minister observed that people are fondly remembering and revisiting his previous 2013 address at the college. He mentioned that the speech created a lasting wave whose positive impact remains completely intact even after 13 to 14 years. “Devoting myself wholeheartedly to the country is the inner passion that manifested in my words that day,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Contrasting past struggles with today's achievements, the Prime Minister emphasized that terrorism has been defeated, with armed forces confidently striking enemies in their own homes and peace restored from Jammu and Kashmir to the Northeast. He highlighted that the world now praises India's policy dynamism and its status as the fastest-growing major economy. “Achieving a 7.8 percent quarterly growth amidst the West Asia war and global trade hurdles demonstrates India's intrinsic capability,” asserted Shri Modi.

Presenting hard economic data to counter persistent critics, the Prime Minister detailed that between April and June, electricity production increased by 9 percent, while overall vehicle sales surged by over 20 percent, driven by a 20 percent growth in two-wheelers and nearly 30 percent in three-wheelers. He argued that an 8 percent increase in steel and cement consumption proves that construction, housing, and commercial activity are rapidly expanding. “Despite this, for the people who saw the glass as half-empty in 2013, their mindset remains exactly the same today,” noted Shri Modi.

Recounting his 2013 promise of Pro-People Good Governance (P2G2), the Prime Minister stated that his government permanently discarded the reactive approach of previous administrations. He cited the 12-year success of the Jan Dhan Yojana as a prime example, recalling that until March 2014, over 50 percent of India's 1.25 billion population lacked bank accounts, whereas the scheme has now integrated around 60 crore citizens. “Today almost every family in the country is connected to the banking system, which has formed the foundation of India's Fintech revolution,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Defending the 'Make in India' initiative against early mockery, the Prime Minister celebrated its monumental success in transforming the nation from a massive importer to a leading exporter. He proudly shared that smartphone exports now exceed Rs 2.5 lakh crore, while domestic defense production has hit an all-time high of nearly Rs 2 lakh crore, turning 2013-14 defense exports of a mere Rs 600-700 crore into a massive Rs 40,000 crore industry today. “I am not a person who walks with small and easy goals; I set huge targets for the country and put my heart and soul into achieving them,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Expressing immense trust in the youth and the capability of 140 crore Indians, the Prime Minister laid out a bold vision for a self-reliant and fully developed India. He outlined ambitious future milestones, including becoming a superpower in agriculture exports, establishing an Indian space station, and eventually hosting the Olympic Games. “And these are not just talks, these are our firm resolutions,” asserted Shri Modi.

Transitioning from the lively campus life of tea at the Co-op, Crossroads, and the Business Conclave to the realities of the outside world, the Prime Minister warned students about cynical individuals who compulsively oppose national progress. He pointed out how these naysayers habitually questioned vital projects like the world's tallest Statue, High-Speed Trains, UPI, and the new Parliament building. “But India gave an answer: no one can stop India from doing what is necessary for the country,” remarked Shri Modi.

Highlighting the unprecedented speed of infrastructure and policy execution, the Prime Minister noted that projects which previously took decades are now being completed in just a few years. He cited that despite India's first electric train running in 1925, less than 30 percent of railway lines were electrified by 2014, whereas his government achieved nearly 100 percent electrification in just 12 years, alongside signing Free Trade Agreements with 40 countries covering leather, textiles, and processed foods. “This is creating a new sky of opportunities for the youth of India,” observed Shri Modi.

Shri Modi recalled his administration's resilient handling of severe modern crises like the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war. “There is so much power in the blessings of the people of my country that every desire of those wishing ill upon India is falling flat,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Encouraging the ambitious spirit of the 21st-century youth, the Prime Minister celebrated their drive to build unicorns, innovate in drone technology, and create cutting-edge AI solutions. He urged them to dream even bigger than previous generations, challenging them to build global consulting, accounting, financial, and legal firms that can lead the world. “Today, Indians are leading the top companies of the world, so why can't companies built by Indians lead the world?” noted Shri Modi.

Drawing inspiration from the SRCC college crest, the Prime Minister beautifully compared the youth's journey to a ship advancing toward a guiding sun. He called upon everyone to navigate a new path of self-reliance where the courage, the dreams, and the ultimate victory belong entirely to India. “On the path to a Viksit Bharat, every rapidly rising step should be ours,” asserted Shri Modi.

 

Delighted to join the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce. Over the years, this institution has given generations of students the opportunity to learn, grow and make a difference.@SRCCOfficial

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM’s address during the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC)
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 9:17PM by PIB Delhi

केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल के मेरे साथी श्रीमान प्रहलाद जोशी जी, डीयू के वीसी योगेश सिंह जी, SRCC की प्रिंसिपल सिमरित कौर जी, अजय जी, मल्लिका जी, रजत जी, SRCC से जुड़े हुए सभी साथी, फैकल्टी, स्टाफ, SRCC alumni और मेरे युवा साथियों!

मैं छठा खिलाड़ी हूं। आज का ये अवसर श्रीराम कॉलेज ऑफ कॉमर्स के लिए  बहुत ऐतिहासिक है, ये देश के शिक्षा जगत के लिए भी उतना ही अहम है। यहां SRCC का हिस्सा रहीं अनेक पीढ़ियां एक साथ जुटी हैं। मैं आप सभी को, SRCC के इस शताब्दी समारोह के लिए बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं। मैं इसके संस्थापक  सर श्रीराम जी को आदरपूर्वक श्रृद्धांजलि देता हूं, उनके विजन को नमन करता हूं।

साथियों,

जब कोई इंसान 100 वर्ष जीता है, तो उसे अनुभवों का सागर माना जाता है। और जब कोई संस्थान 100 वर्ष का होता है, तो वो उपलब्धियों और प्रेरणाओं का महासागर हो जाता है। अपनी 100 वर्षों की इस यात्रा में, SRCC ने पीढ़ियों को गढ़ा है, उन्हें उज्ज्वल भविष्य से जोड़ा है। जो आए उन्होंने पढ़ा, और जो निकले वो गढ़े हुए निकले। इस कॉलेज की यात्रा दरियागंज की, वहां एक छोटे से स्थान से शुरु हुई थी, और आज वही छोटा सा कॉलेज, एक विशाल वृक्ष बन चुका है। एक ऐसा विशाल वृक्ष जिसने कई पीढ़ियों को छांव भी दी है, और अपनी शीतलता से समृद्ध भी किया है। आज भी DU में जब कोई पूछता है कि कौन सा college, तो SRCC कहना ही, SRCC कहना ही अपने आप में ही एक flex होता है।

साथियों,

SRCC के alumni भी बहुत special रहे। अगर मैं आपकी भाषा में कहूं, तो यहां के alumni, OG हैं, जिन्होंने SRCC का नाम दुनिया भर में पहुँचाया, अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों में अपनी एक पहचान बनाई। और रजत जी ने बड़ी लंबी सूची बताई थी। और इनमें से कुछ के साथ मुझे भी काम करने का अवसर मिला है। हमारे अरुण जेटली जी, यहीं पढ़े थे। और मैं कह सकता हूं कि शायद हमारी कोई मुलाकात ऐसी नहीं होती थी, कि वो SRCC की घटना न सुनाते हों। और कभी-कभी मैं तंग आ जाता था, कि एक ही घटना बार-बार सुनाते थे। अभी मेरी टीम में भाई संजीव सान्याल भी, यहीं से पढ़े हुए हैं। बाकी भी काफी साथी हैं यहां मेरे। और ऐसा नहीं है कि यहां से सिर्फ अर्थ-जगत के ही लोग निकले, कितने ही आर्टिस्ट्स से लेकर नेता, वकील, जस्टिस सब यहां से निकले हैं। यानी SRCC के लोगों ने हर क्षेत्र में अपनी धूम मचाई है। धुरंधर न हो लेकिन धूम तो मचाई है।

साथियों,

बीते कुछ दिनों से इस कार्यक्रम की बहुत चर्चा चल रही है। खासतौर पर लोग 2013 के मेरे संबोधन को याद कर रहे हैं। लोगों ने उसको फिर से सुना है, फिर से पढ़ा है, संभव है, इस नई पीढ़ी के लोगों ने भी उसको री-विजिट किया होगा। उस स्पीच के एक प्रकार से मैं कह सकता हूं कि Wave बन गई थी, एक लहर सी चल पड़ी थी। और आज भी, 13-14 साल बाद भी, उस सभा का, उस संबोधन का प्रभाव बरकरार है।

साथियों,

तब आपकी जगह आपके सीनियर बैठे थे। और मैं तब सीएम तो था, लेकिन मैं देश की मुख्य विपक्षी पार्टी का एक सदस्य भी था। और संभवत: तब लोग ये उम्मीद कर रहे थे, कि मैं तब की केंद्र सरकार पर लंबे-चौड़े अटैक करूंगा, आरोपों की झड़ी लगा दूंगा।

लेकिन साथियों,

विपक्ष में होने के बाद भी, तत्कालीन सरकार का आलोचक होने के बावजूद, मैंने  इस मंच का वो उपयोग नहीं किया था, मैंने एक विजन रखा, सकारात्मक बातें कहीं। मैंने तब जो कुछ भी कहा, वो मेरा कन्विक्शन था। मैं उन बातों को, उन सपनों को हमेशा से जीता आया हूँ, उस रास्ते पर ही चलता रहा हूँ, देश के लिए जी-जान से जुटना, देश के लिए जीने का जज्बा, जो मेरे भीतर का भाव-विश्व है, वो उस दिन 2013 में इसी मंच से, मेरा वो भाव-विश्व शब्दों की माला में एक एक करके प्रकट होता चला गया था। और मैं देर तक बोला था फिर मैंने  मैंने स्टूडेंट्स से पूछा कि क्या मैं continue कर दूं, उन्होंने जोर से कहा हाँ continue कीजिए।

साथियों,

मैंने उस दिन पानी के ग्लास का एक उदाहरण दिया था, और देश में उसकी खूब चर्चा भी हुई थी। मैंने बताया था कि पानी से आधे भरे ग्लास को देखने के तीन नज़रिए क्या होते हैं। एक, जिनको ग्लास पानी से आधा भरा दिखता है, दूसरा, जिनको ग्लास आधा खाली दिखता है, और तीसरा, जिनको ग्लास पूरा भरा हुआ दिखता है, आधा पानी और आधा हवा से भरा।

साथियों,

ये वो समय था, जब देश निराशा के दलदल में धंसा हुआ था। मैंने तब भी कहा था, कि मैं ग्लास को आधा नहीं देखता, अधूरा नहीं देखता, गिलास को पूरा भरा हुआ देखता हूं। आधा पानी से, आधा हवा से। और उस समय आप सब तो स्कूल में रहे होंगे, लेकिन आज इंटरनेट पर जाकर के 2013 और उसके आसपास की खबरें अगर  पढ़ेंगे, तो आपको अंदाजा आएगा, तब सिचुएशन क्या थी? और मैं तो आपसे आग्रह करूंगा नौजवानों से, कि जरा 2013 के उस कालखंड की तरफ इंटरनेट पर जाकर के नजर करिए। 2013 में मेरे उस भाषण के आसपास के कालखंड की उस समय जो हेडलाइन्स हुआ करती थीं। अखबारों की हो या टीवी चैनल्स की हो। मैं जरा आज उस हेडलाइन्स में क्या क्या था, उसकी एक झलक आपको दिखाना चाहता हूं। अब एक गैंग है, जो क्या करेगी, मैं जो बोल रहा हूं ना उसके छोटे-छोटे टुकड़े करके मेरे खाते में डाल देगी। और इसलिए मैं पहले से आगाह करता हूं कि मैं जो बातें बता रहा हूं 2013 के उस कालखंड में मीडिया में क्या छाया रहता था जैसे-

  • LoC पर भारतीय सैनिकों की हत्या, अब इस पीढ़ी को जरा अजूबा लगता होगा ऐसा भी होता था। होता था।

  • वर्ल्ड बैंक ने GDP ग्रोथ रेट का अनुमान घटाया

  • करंट अकाउंट डेफिसिट ऑल टाइम हाई

  • महंगाई दर करीब दस परसेंट पर

  • इडस्ट्रियल सेक्टर मंदी की चपेट में

  • हेलीकॉप्टर सौदे में घूसखोरी का पर्दाफाश

  • हैदराबाद में बम धमाके

ये सारी उस समय की हेडलाइन्स थीं। मैं पक्का मानता हूं, ये जो हमारे आज जो विद्यार्थी हैं, उनको इन सारी बातों का पता नहीं होगा। ये सारी बातें बताती हैं कि तब देश की क्या हालत थी। ग्रोथ फर्श पर थी और महंगाई अर्श पर थी। घोटाले चरम पर थे और भ्रष्टाचारी बेखौफ घूमते थे। अर्थव्यवस्था बेहाल थी, चारों तरफ पॉलिसी पैरालिसिस की ही चर्चा थी। दुनिया भारत को फ्रैजाइल फाइव में गिन रही थी। आतंकी बेलगाम थे और पाकिस्तान बेकाबू था। यानी तब निराशा और हताशा के अलावा कुछ नहीं था।

साथियों,

एक वो दिन था जब हर मोर्चे पर, देश में स्ट्रगल ही स्ट्रगल था, और एक आज का दिन है, आज आतंकवाद फैलाने वाले पस्त पड़े हैं। पाकिस्तान कोई नापाक हरकत करता है, तो भारत की सेनाएं घर में घुसकर मारती हैं। जम्मू-कश्मीर से लेकर नॉर्थ ईस्ट तक शांति बढ़ी है। माओवादी आतंक, नक्सलवाद की कमर तोड़ दी गई है। जो दुनिया तब भारत में पॉलिसी पैरालिसिस से चिंतित थी, वो दुनिया आज भारत के पॉलिसी डायनामिज्म की चर्चा कर रही है। तब दुनिया भारत को फ्रजाइल फाइव बता रही थी, आज दुनिया भारत को फास्टेस्ट ग्रोइंग मेजर इकॉनॉमी बनते हुए देख रही है। अभी हफ्तेभर में ही, भारत की इकॉनॉमी को लेकर कई सारी पॉजिटिव खबरें आई हैं। Seven point eight percent क्वाटर्ली ग्रोथ ने देश का जोश बढ़ाया है, और इसी बीच जैपनीज़ Credit Rating Agency ने भारत की रेटिंग अपग्रेड कर दी है।

और साथियों,

ये Seven point eight percent की ग्रोथ भी ऐसे समय में आई है, जब west asia का युद्ध चल रहा है, जब ट्रेड से जुड़ी कई तरह की अड़चनें रही हैं, उस समय ऐसी ग्रोथ हासिल करना, ये अपने आप में भारत के सामर्थ्य को दिखाता है।

साथियों,

मैं जानता हूं, आप भी जानते हैं, जो लोग, भारत को फ्रैजाइल फाइव में धकेलने के लिए बदनाम रहे हैं, उनको ये आंकड़े हज़म नहीं हो रहे हैं। लेकिन आप सभी आंकड़ों को गंभीरता से समझते हैं। अप्रैल से जून के बीच, बिजली उत्पादन, नाइन परसेंट बढ़ा, गाड़ियों की सेल में ट्वेंटी परसेंट से अधिक की वृद्धि हुई। इसमें भी, टू-व्हीलर में, ट्वेंटी परसेंट, और थ्री व्हीलर की बिक्री में करीब करीब थर्टी परसेंट की ग्रोथ रही है। यानी consumer demand भी चल रही है, और commercial activity भी तगड़ी हो रही है। Steel और सीमेंट कंजम्शन की ग्रोथ में 8 परसेंट की वृद्धि हुई है। यानी construction, housing, infrastructure और industrial activity, ये सब बढ़ रहा है। यानी भारत, ग्रो भी कर रहा है, और रोजगार के नए अवसर भी बना रहा है। बावजूद इसके, जिन लोगों के लिए साल 2013 में ग्लास आधा खाली था, उनकी सोच आज भी वैसी ही है। उनके लिए ग्लास हमेशा आधा खाली रहेगा। मैं ग्लास की बात करता हूं, और कुछ खाली रहने की बात नहीं कर रहा हूं।

साथियों,

2013 में यहां SRCC में बात करते हुए, मैंने P2G2 यानी प्रो-पीपल गुड-गवर्नेंस की भी चर्चा की थी। जिन्होंने लंबे समय तक देश में सरकारें चलाई हैं, उनका एक स्टाइल था, जब आग लगे तभी नींद से जागो, जब सूखा पड़े तब जाकर कुआं खोदो। मैंने इसी अप्रोच को बदलने की बात कही थी। और 2014 में सरकार बनने के बाद हमने ये करके दिखाया है। मैं आपको एक उदाहरण देता हूं।

साथियों,

हाल में ही, जनधन योजना को 12 साल पूरे हुए हैं। आज आप फिनटेक के अलग ही दौर में जी रहे हैं, लेकिन 2013 के वो दिन भी थे जब गांव या छोटे शहरों के स्टूडेंट्स को, सेविंग बैंक अकाउंट्स खुलवाने के लिए भी कई पापड़ बेलने प़ड़ते थे। उस समय हमारी आबादी सवा सौ करोड़ के पार थी, लेकिन मार्च 2014 तक, देश की 50 प्रतिशत से ज्यादा आबादी के पास बैंक अकाउंट्स तक नहीं थे। और जो बैंकिंग सिस्टम से बाहर थे, वो ज्यादातर गरीब थे, महिलाएं थीं, माइग्रेंट लेबरर थे, स्टूडेंट्स थे। इसलिए हम जनधन स्कीम लेकर आए, और बीते 12 वर्षों में जनधन योजना की वजह से, करीब 60 करोड़ नए बैंक अकाउंट खुले। आज देश में लगभग हर परिवार बैकिंग सिस्टम से जुड़ा हुआ है। यही भारत की फिनटेक क्रांति का आधार बना है।

साथियों,

अब आप उन लोगों के बारे में भी सोचिए, जो करोड़ों लोगों को बैंकिंग व्यवस्था से जोड़ने का भी विरोध कर रहे थे। दरअसल ऐसे लोगों को, आधे भरे ग्लास में ही मज़ा आता है, ताकि देश के गरीब सामान्य नागरिक उनके आगे-पीछे घूमते रहें, यही माई-बाप कल्चर ये दशकों से चला रहे थे। लेकिन ये मोदी है, माई-बाप कल्चर पसंद करने वालों के सामने वो चट्टान की तरह खड़ा है।

साथियों,

पुरानी कहावत है, सांच को आंच नहीं। मुझमें हिम्मत है, इसीलिए मैं उस दिन कही बातों को याद करा रहा हूं, अपना रिपोर्ट कार्ड लेकर आया हूं आपके पास। मैं जानता हूं, सच की हुंकार के आगे, झूठ की गूंज टिक नहीं सकेगी।

साथियों,

2013 के उसी कार्यक्रम में जब मैंने कहा कि हमें मेड इन इंडिया पर काम करना है, तो पुराने उस समय के इकोसिस्टम के लोगों को ये समझ ही नहीं आया था। उनको लगता था, कि निराशा के उस दौर में मेड इन इंडिया संभव ही नहीं होगा! और उस सोच में पले-बड़े लोग आज भी, मेड इन इंडिया का मजाक करते हैं।

लेकिन साथियों,

आज आप मेक इन इंडिया की ब्रैंड वैल्यू देख रहे हैं। आपसे मैं एक उदाहरण के साथ बात बताना चाहता हूं। आज हर हाथ में स्मार्टफोन है, दुनिया के बड़े से बड़े फोन ब्रैंड, आज भारत को अपना बेस बना रहे हैं। मेड इन इंडिया स्मार्टफोन, दुनिया के कोने-कोने में पहुंच रहा है। 2014 में भारत अपने ज्यादातर मोबाइल फोन इंपोर्ट करता था। आज भारत ढाई लाख करोड़ रुपए से ज्यादा के मोबाइल एक्सपोर्ट करता है।

साथियों,

मैं छोटे और आसान लक्ष्य लेकर चलने वाला व्यक्ति नहीं हूं। मैं देश के लिए बड़े लक्ष्य रखता हूं, और उन्हें पूरा करने के लिए जी-जान लगा देता हूं। आप डिफेंस का सेक्टर देखिए, पहले भारत की सेनाओं के लिए ज्यादातर चीज़ें बाहर से खरीदी जाती थीं। मैंने आते ही डिफेंस वालों को बोला नेगेटिव लिस्ट बनाईये। पहले उन्होंने 500 नेगेटिव लिस्ट बनाई, बोले ये हम बाहर से नहीं लाएंगे। फिर हजार बनाई, फिर तीन हजार बनाई। आर्मी, नेवी, एयरफोर्स को, कई बार छोटे से किसी इक्विप्मेंट के लिए भी महीनों इंतजार करना पड़ता था। हमने देश की सेनाओं के साथ मिलकर एक प्लान बनाया, चीज़ों की लिस्ट बनाई, फिर भारतीय कंपनियों को कहा कि ये सब बनाओ, और आज आप देखिए, देश की डिफेंस मैन्युफैक्चरिंग, अपने ऑल टाइम हाई पर है। आज भारत करीब-करीब 2 लाख करोड़ रुपये का डिफेंस प्रोडक्शन कर रहा है। 2013-14 में, हम 600-700 करोड़ रुपये का डिफेंस एक्सपोर्ट करते थे। आज ये आंकड़ा, करीब-करीब 40 हजार करोड़ रुपये तक पहुंच चुका है। और ये अचीवमेंट्स इसलिए हो पा रहे हैं, क्योंकि आज देश में एक वाइब्रेंट डिफेंस मैन्युफेक्चरिंग इकोसिस्टम बन रहा है।

साथियों,

मुझे देश पर भरोसा है, देश के सामर्थ्य पर भरोसा है, आप युवाओं पर मेरा भरोसा है, और इसी भरोसे के आधार पर मैं विकसित भारत की बात भी कहता हूं। मुझे विश्वास है, हम 140 करोड़ भारतीय मिलकर अपने देश को विकसित भी बनाएंगे, आत्मनिर्भर भी बनाएंगे। 

  • आने वाले समय में, भारत, मैन्यूफैक्चरिंग का हब होगा।

  • आने वाले समय में रिसर्च एंड इनोवेशन का हब हिन्दुस्तान होगा।

  • भारत,एग्रीकल्चर एक्सपोर्ट की सुपर पावर होगा।

मेरे नौजवान दोस्तों,

  • भारत का अपना स्पेस स्टेशन होगा,

  • और वो दिन भी आप देखेंगे, जब भारत एक दिन ऐसे ओलंपिक्स का आयोजन करेगा कि दुनिया देखती रह जाएगी।

और ये केवल बातें नहीं है, ये हमारे संकल्प हैं। और इन संकल्पों को सिद्धि में बदलने के लिए देश में लगातार काम हो रहा है।

साथियों,

अभी तो आपकी ज़िंदगी SRCC मोड में चल रही है। को-ऑप में चाय हो, या cold coffee पर होने वाली discussions हों, exam में last-minute notes, और printouts के लिए भाग-दौड़ करना, या फिर Crossroads और Business Conclave पर की गई मेहनत है, आप सब ने यहाँ के हर मोमेंट को अपने जीवन की एक memory बनाया है। लेकिन इस कैंपस के बाहर एक नई दुनिया आपको मिलेगी। आपको दो तरह के लोग मिलेंगे। एक वो लोग, जो पॉजिटिव तरीके से समाज की शक्ति को राष्ट्र की शक्ति में बदलते हैं। दूसरी प्रजाति उन लोगों की है, जो कोई भी काम शुरू होने पर नाराज़ फूफा बन जाते हैं, उनका फेवरेट काम होता है, हर काम का विरोध करना। इनका एक ही डायलॉग होता है, इसकी क्या ज़रूरत है?, इसकी क्या ज़रूरत है?, ये हर फूफा का परमानेंट डॉयलोग होता है। जब हम दुनिया का सबसे बड़ा Statue बना रहे थे, तो फूफा जी ने कमर कस ली, कहा इसकी ज़रूरत ही क्या है? हमने High-Speed Train पर काम शुरू किया, तो फूफा जी फिर बोले, इसकी ज़रूरत ही क्या है? हम UPI लेकर आए, तो यही फूफा लोग कहते थे - Why UPI? UPI की ज़रूरत ही क्या है? हमने चिप बनाने की बात की, तो फिर कहा गया, कि ज़रूरत ही क्या है? हमने नई पार्लियामेंट बिल्डिंग बनाई, तो ये फिर बोले - इसकी जरूरत ही क्या है? हमने देश के लिए मरने मिटने वाले, सर्वश्रेष्ठ बलिदान देने वाले हमारे वीर सेनानायकों का मेमोरियल बनवाया, फूफा फिर मैदान में आ गए, इसकी क्या जरूरत थी? लेकिन भारत ने ऐसे सारे फूफाओँ को जवाब दिया, जो देश के लिए जरूरी है, वो भारत को करने से कोई रोक नहीं सकता।

साथियों,

आज भारत एक अलग मिजाज के साथ आगे बढ़ रहा है। जो काम पहले दशकों में होता था, अब वो कुछ वर्षों में ही हो रहा है। मैं पूरे Facts के साथ एक और उदाहरण दूंगा। भारत की पहली Electric ट्रेन 1925 में चली थी। आपकी कॉलेज 1926 में शुरू हुई, Electric ट्रेन 1925 में चली थी। 1925 में चली थी ये ट्रेन, इसके बाद 2014 तक, यानी 90 इयर्स, 90 साल में सिर्फ 30 परसेंट से भी कम काम हुआ। 30 परसेंट से भी कम रेलवे लाइनों का इलेक्ट्रिफिकेशन हो पाया था। हमने सिर्फ 12 साल में, 12 साल में रेलवे लाइनों का करीब-करीब Hundred Percent इलेक्ट्रिफिकेशन करके दिखा दिया।

साथियों,

भारत की नीति-निर्णयों में आई ये गति दुनिया के बाकी देश भी देख रहे हैं, समझ रहे हैं। इसलिए वो भारत के साथ अपनी पार्टनरशिप बढ़ा रहे हैं। बीते दशक में करीब 40 देशों के साथ व्यापार समझौते हुए हैं, Free Trade Agreement हुए हैं। इससे लेदर हो, टेक्स्टाइल हो, फ्रूट-वेजिटेबल हो, हमारा प्रोसेस्ड फूड हो, श्रिंप हो, ऐसी हर चीज के लिए नए-नए बाज़ार खुल रहे हैं। आपसे बेहतर कौन जानता है कि जब नए बाज़ार खुलते हैं, भारत के गुड्स और सर्विसेज़ के लिए टैरिफ कम होते हैं, तो उसका क्या मतलब होता है। ये भारत के नौजवानों के लिए, अवसरों का नया आसमान बन रहा है।

साथियों,

आज 2013 के मुकाबले, देश आर्थिक रूप से, सामाजिक रूप से कहीं अधिक सुरक्षित है। लेकिन ये देखकर कुछ लोगों की छटपटाहट बढ़ रही है, बौखलाहट बढ़ रही है। अभी 15 अगस्त का मेरा भाषण आपने सुना होगा, ऐसे लोगों के लिए अभी मैंने लाल किले से, एक होम्योपैथी का डोज दिया था, होम्योपैथी की गोली एक छोटी सी गोली दी थी लाल किले से, और आप जानते हैं होम्योपैथी के कहते हैं कि स्वभाव ऐसा है कि होम्योपैथी की दवाई जब शुरू करते हैं, तो शुरू के दौर में बीमारी एक दम से ज्यादा बढ़ जाती है, ये होम्योपैथी का स्वभाव है। तो मैंने लाल किले से एक होम्योपैथी की गोली दी थी - दिमाग़ी नक्सल। ये दिमागी नक्सल होम्योपैथी का इलाज, जैसा मैंने कहा बीमारी को कुछ समय के लिए और उभार देता है। और उसके बाद उसका इलाज शुरू करता है। इसी तरह जैसे ही मैंने दिमाग़ी नक्सल वाली होम्योपैथी की गोली दी, सारे दिमागी नक्सल निकल-निकल के बाहर आने लगे। और जो इस बीमारी को बढ़ावा दे रहे हैं, अब जनता उनका भी असली रंग देख रही है।

साथियों,

मैंने इतनी सारी बातें बताईं, कुछ लोगों को लग सकता है, अरे क्या है भाई, 140 करोड़ का देश है, बहुत आसान था, मोदी ने क्या नया किया? लेकिन क्या ये वाकई इतना आसान था? मैं आपको फिर एक बार पुराने दिनों में ले जाना चाहता हूं। याद कीजिए आप जब स्कूल में पढ़ते होंगे। 2013 में केदारनाथ में आपदा आई थी। तो पूरी सरकार हिल गई थी। उनको समझ ही नहीं आ रहा था कि, क्या किया जाए? कैसे किया जाए? 2008 में बैंकों का संकट आया था, तो तब की सरकार ने 2014 तक उस संकट के पीछे छुपने की कोशिश की थी, हाथ तक लगाने की हिम्मत नहीं की। भारत का पूरा बैंकिंग सिस्टम, तबाह होने के कगार पर पहुंचा दिया गया था। 2008 में ही मुंबई में भयंकर आतंकी हमला हुआ था, तो तब की सरकार पर बाहर से दबाव पड़ा, और उसने पाकिस्तान को सबक सिखाने की हिम्मत तक नहीं दिखाई।

साथियों,

पिछले 12 वर्षों में तो देश में कई सारी आपदाएं आईं, इतने बड़े-बड़े साइक्लोन हमने झेलें हैं, लेकिन देश ने बहुत मजबूती से उनका सामना किया। पिछले 6 वर्षों में तो बहुत बड़े संकट आए हैं। पहले कोरोना जैसी महामारी आई, जिसने पूरी दुनिया को ठप कर दिया। फिर रूस और यूक्रेन में युद्ध छिड़ गया। उसके बाद, ट्रेड को, सप्लाई चैन को ही वेपनाइज करने का दौर शुरु हो गया। फिर वेस्ट एशिया का ये संकट आया, हर बार ये कहा गया कि अब तो भारत नहीं बचेगा और जो मेरे ज्यादा ही प्रशंसक हैं, वो ये सोचकर खुश थे कि अब तो मोदी फंसा, अब तो मोदी गिरा, अब तो उसे कुचल ही देंगे, लेकिन मेरे देश के लोगों के आशीर्वाद में इतना दम है, इतना दम है कि, भारत का बुरा चाहने वालों की हर हसरत धरी की धरी रह जा रही है।

दोस्तों,

अब 21वीं सदी में नए अवसरों की दुनिया हमारे सामने है। मुझे खुशी है कि आप ambitious हैं, क्योंकि ambition किसी textbook से नहीं सिखाई जा सकती। Ambitions उस माहौल से आती है, जो आपको बड़े सपने देखने के लिए आपको प्रेरित करती है। आज हमारा नौजवान साथी कहता है कि अपना कुछ काम करुंगा, तो स्टार्ट-अप करुंगा, कंपनी बनाऊँगा, तो unicorn बनाऊँगा। स्पेस और ड्रोन जैसे सेक्टर में जुडूंगा, कुछ बड़ा करूंगा। Cutting-edge AI सोल्यूशन्स बनाऊँगा, खेती में इनोवेशन करूंगा। 13 साल पहले आपके सीनियर्स, ऐसे सपने नहीं देख पाते थे। लेकिन आज आप ये सपने भी देख रहे हैं, क्योंकि आज के भारत में उन सपनों को सपोर्ट करने वाला इकोसिस्टम भी बन गया है।

साथियों,

अब समय बड़े लक्ष्य बनाने और उन्हें प्राप्त करने का है। अभी मैंने लाल किले से कुछ बातें कहीं थीं। मैं आपके बीच भी उन्हें दोहराना चाहूंगा। आप संकल्प लीजिए, भारत की global consulting firms क्यों नहीं हो सकतीं? हमारी accounting Firms, हमारी legal firms, हमारी financial firms, ये सब global leaders क्यों नहीं बन सकतीं? हम गर्व से कहते हैं कि आज भारतीय दुनिया की टॉप कंपनीज़ को लीड कर रहे हैं, अगर भारतीय दुनिया की टॉप कंपनियों को लीड कर रहे हैं, तो भारतीयों की बनाई कंपनियां, दुनिया को क्यों लीड न करें?

साथियों,

ये सब संभव है, इसके लिए आपके पास networks भी हैं और knowledge भी है।

साथियों,

हमारी आपकी प्रेरणा SRCC का ये कॉलेज क्रेस्ट भी है। इसमें दो सुंदर प्रतीक हैं। एक है- उगता हुआ सूरज, और दूसरा है - समुद्र में आगे बढ़ता हुआ जहाज। सूरज, जो दिशा दिखाता है और जहाज, जो उस दिशा में आगे बढ़ता है। हमें ऐसे नए रास्ते पर चलना है, जिसमें सूरज हमारा हो, समंदर भी हमारा हो। नाव हमारी हो, नाविक भी हमारा हो। लहरों पर विजय लिखे, वो हौसला हमारा हो। उड़ान हमारी हो, आसमान हमारा हो। तेज हवाओं से टकराए, वो जज़्बा हमारा हो। सपना हमारा हो, संकल्प हमारा हो, आत्मनिर्भर भारत का परचम हमारा हो। विकसित भारत की राह में, विकसित भारत की राह में तेजी से उठता हर कदम हमारा हो। एक बार फिर इस विशेष अवसर पर SRCC से जुड़े सभी लोगों को मेरी ढेर सारी शुभकामनाएँ।

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2 Inaugurated
Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal inaugurates the corridor in the presence of Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Mohan Yadav
Metro network expands to 16 operational stations covering approximately 17 km
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal, in the presence of Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Shri Mohan Yadav, today inaugurated the Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2, marking a significant milestone in the city’s urban mobility journey. Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Tokhan Sahu was also present on the occasion.

The newly inaugurated phase-I (Reach-II) of approx 11 km comprising 11-stations  starting from Super Corridor-3 to Malviya Nagar Chauraha and has been developed at an estimated cost of ₹2,850 crore. With this expansion, the Indore Metro network now comprises 16 operational stations covering approximately 17 km, with a cumulative project cost of about ₹4,370 crore.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Manohar Lal said that the Metro will provide citizens with a faster, safer, more comfortable and reliable mode of transport while strengthening connectivity between residential, commercial and employment centres.

The Union Minister emphasised that Metro Rail is not merely a transportation project but an important instrument for economic growth, urban transformation and social inclusion. Increased use of public transport will also help reduce traffic congestion, fuel consumption and emissions.

Shri Manohar Lal congratulated the Government of Madhya Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Limited, officials, engineers, workers and all stakeholders associated with the project.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NCSC Seeks Time Bound Response Over Complaint Regarding Denial Of Reservation Benefits To SC Candidates In The Recruitment Process For Lecturer Posts
Notice Issued To Chief Secretary Of Punjab Government, Response Sought Within Seven Days
NCSC Chairman Kishor Makwana describes ‘denial of reservation benefits to SC candidates in the recruitment process a very serious matter’
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

Exercising the powers conferred under Article 338 of the Constitution of India, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) has ordered inquiry into the matter connected to a representation from Shri Tarun Chugh, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) wherein he has alleged non-implementation of the reservation policy in the recruitment of Lecturers in the Punjab Education Department.

The representation complains that Scheduled Caste candidates have been denied the benefits of reservation in the recruitment process for 1,013 Lecturer posts notified by the Punjab Education Department.

In this regard, a notice has been issued to the Chief Secretary of the Punjab Government, directing him to submit to the Commission, within seven days of receipt of the notice, the facts of the case, the action taken on the allegations, and all related records (including the recruitment notification and the reservation roster).

It is alleged that in several subjects (Punjabi, Commerce, Mathematics, Physics, Economics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography, etc.), the reservation rules and the prescribed roster system have not been properly followed.

The National Commission for Scheduled Castes has also clarified that if a response is not received within the stipulated time limit, it may, under Article 338 of the Constitution, exercise the powers of a civil court and issue summons for personal appearance.

The Chairman of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, Shri Kishor Makwana, stated that the denial of reservation benefits to Scheduled Caste candidates in the recruitment process for Lecturer posts is a very serious matter.

He said that the Commission is committed to protecting the constitutional rights of Scheduled Castes and to ensuring strict compliance with reservation provisions in government services. The Commission will take all necessary steps in accordance with the law to ensure justice.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President releases commemorative postage stamp marking 75 years of Dinamalar in Chennai
Dinamalar has earned people’s trust by upholding truth, patriotism and public service: Vice President
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today said that Dinamalar has earned the trust of the people over the past 75 years by upholding the values of truth, patriotism and public service, and called upon the newspaper to continue serving the nation for many more years.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan released a commemorative postage stamp marking the 75th year of Dinamalar in Chennai today.

He lauded Dinamalar’s 7-decade-long journey of upholding truth, patriotism and public service. pic.twitter.com/up4o6RTNKK

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 5, 2026


Addressing the function held in Chennai to mark the 75th year of publication of Dinamalar and the release of a commemorative postage stamp, the Vice President noted that Dinamalar, founded in 1951 with the resolve to serve as a touchstone of truth and Recalled the contribution of Dinamalar founder Shri T. V. Ramasubbaiyer.

He observed that an idea that originated in the mind of one individual has today grown into a large organisation, reflecting the dedication and collective efforts of successive generations.

Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan emphasised that a newspaper can earn and retain the trust of the people only when it stands firm against pressures and continues to uphold higher values such as patriotism and public service without fear.He said that Dinamalar’s work over the past 75 years has established such a bond of trust with its readers.

The Vice President stressed the importance of nurturing the next generation and appreciated Dinamalar’s efforts through its ‘Pattam’ publication, which brings knowledge on general awareness, language skills and scientific innovations to school students.

The Vice President wished Dinamalar continued growth and success, saying that it should remain a touchstone of truth, serving the nation and society for many more decades.

The function was attended by Chennai Regional Director of the Department of Posts, Major Manoj; Editor of the Dinamalar Group, Dr. R. Ramasubbu; publishers Shri L. Aadhimoolam, Dr. L. Ramasubbu and Smt. Jayashree; Shri R. R. Gopalji, and other distinguished guests.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Biodiversity Authority Crosses ₹200-Crore Milestone in ABS Disbursement
₹8.23 crore in Access and Benefit-Sharing proceeds to be disbursed to States and UTs from utilisation of four key vegetable crops
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has crossed a significant milestone in the implementation of India’s Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) framework, with cumulative ABS disbursements exceeding ₹200 crore. As part of this continuing effort, the NBA has sanctioned ₹8.23 crore in ABS proceeds to 27 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and 5 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs), arising from the access and utilisation of biological resources associated with Bitter Gourd (Momordica charantia), Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), Chilli (Capsicum annuum) and Onion (Allium cepa).

The ABS proceeds were realised from seed companies M/s Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd., M/s East West Seeds India Pvt. Ltd. and M/s Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd. in connection with access to these biological resources for research and commercial utilisation.

The biological resources had been accessed through the open market or through traders and hence could not be traced to specific individual farmers, communities or a single identifiable geographic source. Accordingly, in accordance with the modality recommended by the Expert Committee and approved by the Authority, the beneficiary share is being distributed among the SBBs/UTBCs of the States and Union Territories where the respective crops are cultivated.

The distribution is based on the area under cultivation, as published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. This approach enables the ABS proceeds to be channelled towards States and Union Territories associated with the cultivation of the respective biological resources, where direct identification of the individual providers or source communities is not possible.

Among the States and UTs receiving the ABS proceeds, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra emerge as the largest cumulative recipients across the four crops. Madhya Pradesh's share is supported by its cultivation of Bitter Gourd, Chilli and Onion, while Maharashtra's position is primarily attributed to its significant share of India's Onion cultivation area, accounting for more than 49 per cent. The combined ABS amounts payable to the ten largest recipient States/UTs across the four crops are as follows:

The SBBs/UTBCs are required to utilise the funds for activities enumerated under Section 32(2) of the Biological Diversity Act 2002, including documentation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers (PBRs), in-situ and ex-situ conservation of biological resources, restoration of degraded ecosystems, strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites, capacity building of Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) and enhancement of community livelihoods.

The latest disbursement marks another important step in India's efforts to ensure that benefits arising from the utilisation of biological resources are channelled towards biodiversity conservation and associated community-oriented activities.

The cumulative ABS disbursement of more than ₹200 crore underscores the continued efforts of the NBA to strengthen implementation of the Biological Diversity Act and operationalise the principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of biological resources. The initiative also contributes to India's commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing, as well as the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), particularly Target 13, which calls for effective measures to ensure fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources, as applicable.

The program centered on the implementation of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) Standard Framework for the paving and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-CRRI Conducts Specialized Training for PWD Delhi Engineers on CAQM Standard Framework for Paving and Greening of Urban Roads
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

The CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CRRI) organized a specialized training program for engineers of the Public Works Department (PWD), Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD), at the NDMC Convention Centre. The program centered on the implementation of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) Standard Framework for the paving and greening of urban roads across the National Capital Territory.

The inaugural ceremony commenced with a traditional lamp lighting and formal welcome of dignitaries. The Director of CRRI Dr.Ch.Ravi Sekhar delivered the inaugural address alongside addresses by the Sh.Naveen Bansal, Engineer-in-Chief (EinC), PWD, and Sh. Ravi Jha, Special Secretary-2, PWD. The address underscored the critical role of scientific road design, environmental mitigation, and standard paving techniques in curbing road dust and improving Delhi's overall air quality.

The comprehensive one-day training schedule covered technical and field-level planning modules led by CRRI domain experts and Scientists including Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Dr.Sampath Kumar, Dr. K. Ravinder, Dr. E. Madhu, Dr. Mukti Advani, Dr. Minal Chandra, Dr. Chintaman Bari and Dr. Nischal Gupta.

  • Framework Background & Principles: In-depth orientation on the background of paving and greening guidelines in the NCR region, principles of urban space standards, and road network planning aligned with IRC guidelines to enhance environment and safety.
  • Carriageway Design & Data Formats: Technical guidance on carriageway standards for various categories of urban roads along with standard data collection formats.
  • Transit & Non-Motorized Transport (NMT): Engineering benchmarks for public transport facility design, alongside dedicated standards for pedestrian walkways and non-motorized transport.
  • Safety & Infrastructure Integration: Technical sessions detailing road signs and markings, as well as seamless integration of essential urban utilities—including drainage, electric utilities, telecom networks, bus stops, and gas fuel stations.

The session concluded with an interactive discussion between CRRI Scientists and participating PWD engineers to outline the operational roadmap and way forward for field-level implementation across the capital's road network.

P. Radhakrishnan, today launched the India Valve…
item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
VICE PRESIDENT LAUNCHES INDIA VALVE REGISTRY AT INDIA VALVES 2026 IN CHENNAI
India Valve Registry to strengthen evidence-based cardiac care: Vice President
India must generate its own clinical evidence for better patient care: Vice President
Healthcare is a human right ,Medical advancements must be inclusive and accessible to all: Vice President
A Viksit Bharat must also be a Swasth Bharat: Vice President
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today launched the India Valve Registry at India Valves 2026, a national academic meeting dedicated to advancing the treatment of valvular and structural heart diseases, in Chennai.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan launched the India Valve Registry during the India Valves 2026 conference in Chennai.

He highlighted the importance of generating India-specific clinical evidence to strengthen cardiac research, improve medical decision-making and enhance… pic.twitter.com/1NLbaZy0E5

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 5, 2026

Addressing leading cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers and medical experts from India and abroad, the Vice President said that the coming together of clinical expertise, scientific inquiry, innovation and collaboration represents an important step in the service of humanity.

He underlined that behind every medical procedure, clinical decision and scientific advancement is ultimately a human being, a patient who wishes to live longer, healthier and with dignity.

Highlighting the remarkable advances made in cardiovascular medicine, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan noted that while valvular and structural heart diseases remain an important and growing challenge, advances in medical science have transformed the way these conditions are treated.

He emphasised that every advancement in medical science brings with it a new responsibility to ensure that its benefits are inclusive and accessible to all. He said that healthcare is a human right and should be accessible to everyone.

The Vice President described the launch of the India Valve Registry as an important step in this direction. He said that a valve registry, by systematically recording information on patients undergoing heart valve interventions, their treatment and outcomes over time, can transform individual clinical experiences into collective medical knowledge.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan stressed the importance of generating India-specific clinical evidence. He noted that several countries have developed national registries for advanced valve interventions and other cardiovascular procedures and welcomed efforts to establish such a collaborative initiative in India.

He said that such registries would help create “our country’s own data for our own countrymen” and would enable the medical community to better understand outcomes, identify challenges and gaps, learn from experience and improve patient care.

The Vice President highlighted India’s growing stature as a centre of medical expertise and innovation. Referring to India’s achievements during the COVID-19 pandemic, he said that the country not only developed vaccines for its own people but also supplied vaccines to around 100 countries, demonstrating India’s growing medical and technological capabilities.

“Our doctors, scientists and healthcare professionals have earned respect across the world. India has demonstrated remarkable capabilities in advanced medical treatment,” he said.

Referring to the national goal of building a Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that a developed India must also be a Swasth Bharat.

Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan called for collective efforts to build a healthcare ecosystem in which innovation, technology and scientific progress are ultimately measured by their ability to improve human lives.

The event was attended by Tamil Nadu Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Thiru K. G. Arunraj; Senior Interventional Cardiologist, Apollo hospitals, Chennai, Dr. G. Sengottuvelu;  Chairman, Cardiac Sciences, Fortis Escorts Heart Institute, New Delhi, Dr Ashok Seth; Chairman, Interventional Cardiology, Medanta–The Medicity, Gurugram, Dr. Praveen Chandra, besides eminent cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers, scientists and members of the organising committee.

About India Valves 2026 & India Valve Registry

India Valves 2026 is a national academic meeting on valvular and structural heart disease, bringing together leading cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, researchers and healthcare professionals from across the country and abroad for scientific exchange, training and collaborative research.

The India Valve Registry is a collaborative multicentre initiative for systematic, secure and de-identified collection of real-world data on transcatheter valve interventions across India, aimed at strengthening India-specific clinical evidence and improving patient care.

Kalaiselvi, inaugurates sustainable phase of the Hub Hub has facilitated over 20 technology transfers and supported commercialisation of affordable medical technologies Rural health workers trained under the Hub take affordable diagnostic technologies to underserved communities Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi The…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
DSIR-CRTDH on Affordable Healthcare at IIT Kharagpur enters sustainable phase, strengthens lab-to-market translation and last-mile healthcare delivery
Secretary, DSIR and Director General, CSIR, Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, inaugurates sustainable phase of the Hub
Hub has facilitated over 20 technology transfers and supported commercialisation of affordable medical technologies
Rural health workers trained under the Hub take affordable diagnostic technologies to underserved communities
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Sustainable Phase of the Common Research and Technology Development Hub (CRTDH) on Affordable Healthcare at IIT Kharagpur was inaugurated today by Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and Director General, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), at the Ben Gupta Auditorium, IIT Kharagpur.

Established in 2019 under the CRTDH Scheme of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India, the CRTDH on Affordable Healthcare has successfully completed its initial grant-supported phase and has transitioned into a sustainable phase. The Hub is now operating as a self-sustaining national facility for affordable healthcare technology development and translation, meeting its operational costs through user fees, industry sponsorships and translational partnerships, while continuing to provide infrastructure and technical support to innovators. The facility will continue to provide state-of-the-art infrastructure, technical expertise, and technology development support to MSMEs, startups, innovators, and other stakeholders. The transition of the CRTDH to a self-sustaining model marks an important milestone in strengthening industry–academia collaboration, technology translation, and innovation-led healthcare solutions, while ensuring the continued availability of shared research and technology development infrastructure. The programme was organised as part of the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur.

Chief guest of the event, Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, DSIR and DG, CSIR, in her address emphasised the role of DSIR and the network of CRTDHs in enabling MSMEs, start-ups and individual innovators to strengthen indigenous capability in medical technology. She said that the continued functioning of a CRTDH beyond the period of DSIR support demonstrates the intended outcome of the programme i.e. to serve industry and innovators in a self-sustaining mode. She emphasised that wider utilisation of these facilities would contribute to strengthening the country's indigenous technological capabilities, advancing self-reliance in medical device technologies, and supporting the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India for Viksit Bharat 2047.

On this occasion, Dr. (Mrs.) Kalaiselvi visited the CRTDH wet and dry laboratories and the THRIVE Centre along with Prof. Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur, (Principal Investigator, CRTDH) and DSIR officials. Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi planted a sapling on the IIT Kharagpur campus, symbolising the beginning of the sustainable phase of the DSIR-CRTDH at IIT Kharagpur and reaffirming the commitment towards its continued growth, sustainability, and long-term contribution to innovation and technology development.

Presenting the journey of the Hub from 2019 to 2026, Prof. Suman Chakraborty highlighted the importance of frugal innovation in addressing the constraints faced in real-world healthcare delivery. He stated that designing technologies for use in settings without sophisticated infrastructure and by frontline health workers requires engineering solutions that are robust and accessible. Operating from a 5,000-square-foot facility, the CRTDH has facilitated over 20 technology transfers, many already commercialised, and has partnered with clinical and non-governmental organisations to establish rural health units to support the deployment of affordable healthcare technologies through rural health units.

During the MSME Voices session, enterprises mentored by the CRTDH shared their experiences while translating laboratory prototypes into commercial products. The participating enterprises were felicitated by the Chief Guest and the Director, IIT Kharagpur. Fifteen frontline health workers from remote villages, including the Sundarbans and Birbhum, shared their experiences of deploying affordable diagnostic technologies at the community level. Trained and certified under the Hub’s skilling programmes, in line with the objectives of Skill India, these health workers are now operating rural health units alongside the health delivery structures under the National Health Mission. Through these units, the trained health workers support screening, referral and follow-up services for communities where access to diagnostic facilities remains limited or intermittent.

Dr. Vipin Shukla, Scientist ‘G’ and Head of the CRTDH Scheme of DSIR, whose guidance has been instrumental in the development of the CRTDH initiative, was also acknowledged on the occasion. Dr. Ranjeet Bairwa, Scientist ‘F’ and Member Secretary – CRTDH, DSIR, and Dr. Kailash Petkar, Scientist ‘D’, DSIR, who closely monitored the implementation of the project, were also present during the event and participated in the proceedings. Continued association of the DSIR-CRTDH team with the project was duly acknowledged, followed by a screening of the CRTDH film.

The proceedings highlighted the convergence of frugal technology, local skilling and public health delivery as an important pathway for achieving the objectives of Viksit Bharat to the last mile. The initiative demonstrates how self-reliance in medical devices, employment opportunities for rural youth and equitable access to healthcare can be addressed through an integrated innovation and delivery ecosystem. At the end, the DSIR officials were felicitated by the Director, IIT, Kharagpur. The proceedings were coordinated by Mr. Sohom Banerjee, Project Manager, CRTDH, IIT Kharagpur.

Approximately 200 participants attended the program, including Senior Officers of DSIR, delegates from chambers of commerce and MSME associations, officials of Government MSME development institutions, MSMEs, start-ups, innovators, clinical partners, rural health workers, faculties, researchers, and students of the Institute. Technologies developed at the CRTDH and products commercialised by partner enterprises were exhibited during the event, providing an opportunity for participants to interact with the innovators.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Coal India Output and Dispatch Set to Accelerate as Monsoon Effect Wanes
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi

As the intense rains over coal command regions show clear signs of easing, coal production and supplies at Coal India Limited (CIL) are gathering pace and are set to improve further from here on. Despite prolonged spells of rain through July and August, particularly across the East-Central parts, CIL maintained a steady supply run. During April–August of the current fiscal, CIL supplied 322.90 million Tonnes (MT) of coal, 6.70% higher than the 302.60 MT supplied during the corresponding period last year.

The easing rainfall is already bringing relief on the ground. Coal beds that had turned sticky and wet after prolonged rain exposure are now drying out, making freshly mined coal free-flowing and considerably easier to transfer, handle and dispatch through Coal Handling Plants (CHPs). Coal seams at lower mine horizons that had been submerged are being restored to production through augmented pumping, while repair of internal haul roads is progressing in full swing.

Mines across CIL are consequently stepping up preparations to return to full operational pace, with the focus firmly on ensuring that production and coal movement pick up quickly as ground conditions continue to improve. While average daily coal production during the rain-affected first three days of September stood at around 1.36 MT per day, it rose to approximately 1.7 MT per day  on 04.09.2026, even with just a single day's respite from rain.

Overburden Removal (OBR) – a key indicator of coal bed exposure and future production readiness – has also started gaining momentum. Average daily OBR during the first three days of September stood at 2.5 Million Cubic Metres, improving to 4.1 Million Cubic Metres on 04.09.2026. This improvement in OB removal, together with drying mine conditions, is expected to lend further impetus to production and supplies in the days ahead.

CIL supplied 60.60 MT of coal in August FY 2026–27, registering a 5.50% increase over supplies in August last year. Supplies to the power sector in August 2026 also rose 4.5% to 48.46 MT, compared to August 2025. CIL continues to hold a stock cushion of 76 MT of coal at its pitheads, along with 46 MT of ready-to-mine coal exposure. Average daily dispatch to the power sector, at around 1.35 MT over the first three days of September, has since improved to 1.5 MT on 4th September. Driven by the coal fraternity's commitment to the larger national cause, dispatch to evacuation points is set to see a marked step-up in the coming days through enhanced production and transportation.

With drier conditions setting in, geo-technical concerns around dump and bench stability – and the associated safety risks that intensify during rain – stand considerably reduced, allowing the workforce to operate unhindered at ground zero. To ensure a streamlined flow of coal, CIL subsidiaries have used the lean period to augment their CHP-Silo mechanisms, and with the dry season approaching, rail tracks at loading points and yards are being cleared. Companies such as NCL and SECL have also created additional crushing capacity that will prove valuable in the near term.

The spell of incessant rain has largely passed, and any intermittent showers going forward are not expected to materially affect mining operations.

Alternate modes offered to augment supplies

In view of the availability of adequate coal stock at various sources across the subsidiary companies of Coal India Limited (CIL), and with a view to augmenting coal supplies to the power sector, CIL has offered power plants having Fuel Supply Agreements (FSAs) with Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries to lift additional quantities of coal, including quantities over and above the applicable Annual Contracted Quantities, through road mode, in addition to the existing rail mode, as per the applicable provisions of their respective Fuel Supply Agreements.

With dry spells setting in, loading is expected to pick up further over the coming days. Close monitoring is being maintained to sustain this trend.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President to visit Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh from September 6 to 9
Posted On: 05 SEP 2026 3:30PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, will undertake a four-day visit to Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh from September 6 to 9, 2026.

During his visit, the Vice-President will participate in a series of academic, cultural and public engagements, besides visiting institutions of historical, social and national significance.

On September 6, the Vice-President will arrive in Guwahati, Assam. He will attend the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Geetanagar College, formerly known as Kanya Mahavidyalaya. He will later attend the Convocation Ceremony of Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences (SSUHS), Guwahati.

On September 7, the Vice-President will attend a foundation stone laying programme at Gauhati University, followed by an interaction with students, faculty members and leading citizens at the University’s Convention Centre. He will thereafter proceed to Shillong, Meghalaya, where he will attend a public reception and cultural programme at Soso Tham Auditorium.

On September 8, the Vice-President will visit Imphal, Manipur. He will visit the INA Museum and War Memorial at Moirang and Sainik School Imphal. He will thereafter proceed to Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh.

On September 9, the Vice-President will attend a special session of the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly and visit the Assembly Gallery-cum-Museum. He will also visit Nyedar Namlo , Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum in Itanagar and the Donyi Polo Mission School for the hearing and visually impaired.
