item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Department of Social Justice & Empowerment and Ramakrishna Mission Sign MoU to Strengthen Intergenerational Bonds Across Three Generations
Nationwide Initiative to Cover 200 Pilot Schools and Bring Children, Parents and Grandparents Closer
‘When Every Generation Walks Together, the Nation Moves Forward’  Says Union Minister Shri Virendra Kumar
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Ramakrishna Math & Ramakrishna Mission (RKM), at Ramakrishna Mission, in National Capital today.

The aim of signing of MoU is to implement ‘Creating Intergenerational Bonding’, a nationwide initiative aimed at strengthening the emotional and cultural connection among children, parents and grandparents through the school system.

The MoU was signed in the presence of Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar, Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B.L. Verma, Joint Secretary, DoSJE, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N. and Director, DoSJE Ms Kajal Singh and RKM Secretary Swami Sarvalokananda along with senior officials of both the organizations.

The signing of the MoU reaffirms the Government’s commitment to respect for elders and inclusive development for every generation, reflecting the Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision that ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ is complete only when every generation moves forward together.

Addressing the gathering, Dr Virendra Kumar said that the families are the foundation of our society and this collaboration with Ramakrishna Mission will help our children, parents and grandparents rediscover the value of togetherness. He added that every generation must walk together for the nation to move forward, which is the true spirit of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas.’

 

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B.L. Verma said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, our government remains committed to strengthening family bonds across the country. He said the MoU with Ramakrishna Mission will help create a replicable model that brings three generations closer together through our schools.

RKM Secretary Swami Sarvalokananda said that Ramakrishna Mission believed in service through education and character-building adding that the Mission is glad to partner with the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment to help families rediscover the wisdom of their elders and pass on shared values to the next generation.

In his opening remarks, Joint Secretary, DoSJE, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N. outlined the Department’s vision for the initiative and welcomed the collaboration with Ramakrishna Mission as a step towards building sustainable, school-based models of family engagement.

 

In his Vote of Thanks, an official from Ramakrishna Mission extended gratitude to the Ministry for its support and to all the dignitaries for gracing the occasion.

The MoU provides for research into the intergenerational challenges faced by modern-day families through qualitative studies covering 50 representative schools across four regions of the country. It also includes the design, pilot-testing and finalisation of 20 evidence-based Co-Learning Games for use in schools.

A bilingual English-Hindi Resource Centre website will be developed to support teachers in conducting sessions. The initiative will also include certification training for teachers and the roll-out of Co-Learning Game sessions across 200 pilot schools nationwide.

An independent assessment study will evaluate the outcomes of the initiative and inform its future scale-up across the country.

The initiative builds on the Ministry’s existing senior citizen welfare ecosystem, including the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY). It is designed to enable elders to pass on wisdom and values, parents to bridge tradition and modernity, and children to grow up rooted in culture while feeling emotionally secure.

Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission, an institution inspired by the teachings of Sri Ramakrishna Paramhans and Swami Vivekananda and backed by over a century of service in education, health, culture and humanitarian work, will serve as the implementing partner for the initiative. A Knowledge Development Partner will support the research, design and assessment components.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Hardship to Sanitation Entrepreneurship: Chetan Kumar Kaushik's Journey towards Self-Reliance under NAMASTE-SUY
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Chetan Kumar Kaushik, a 32-year-old resident of Sahibabad in Ghaziabad district, Uttar Pradesh, has transformed years of financial hardship into a journey of self-reliance and dignity. Educated up to the 12th standard, Chetan provides sewer and septic tank suction services in the Mohan Nagar and Sahibabad areas under Nagar Nigam Ghaziabad's Mohan Nagar Zone.

For years, sanitation-related work remained Chetan's primary source of livelihood. Despite working continuously, his limited earnings were largely spent on household expenses and family responsibilities, leaving little scope for savings, business expansion or long-term financial security.

His difficulties increased when his mother became seriously ill and required prolonged medical care. As the sole earning member of the family, Chetan bore the responsibility of supporting his homemaker wife and arranging his mother's treatment. He used the savings generated through his sanitation work to secure treatment for her at reputed hospitals. Despite his efforts, his mother passed away in 2022. The experience was both emotionally devastating and financially demanding, but Chetan continued to fulfil his responsibilities with determination.

A decisive change came through the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) component of the NAMASTE scheme. Chetan received financial assistance, including an upfront capital subsidy, to strengthen and expand his sanitation service enterprise.

The project, with a total cost of Rs. 8.90 lakh, was supported through a loan of Rs. 5,42,500 and a capital subsidy of Rs. 3,47,500. The assistance enabled him to strengthen his suction-machine operations and provide improved sanitation services across areas under the Mohan Nagar Zone.

With better equipment and an expanded livelihood base, Chetan's monthly income increased to approximately Rs. 40,000-Rs. 50,000. The intervention brought greater stability to his household finances, enhanced his capacity to meet family responsibilities and helped him move towards financial independence.

Chetan currently pays a monthly loan instalment of Rs. 12,100. With only around Rs. 67,000 remaining outstanding, he expects to repay the loan fully by October 2026.

Today, Chetan continues to operate his sanitation service enterprise successfully. The scheme has not only improved his income but also strengthened his confidence, independence and social dignity.

His journey demonstrates how timely financial assistance and livelihood support can help sanitation workers overcome economic barriers and build sustainable enterprises. Through resilience, hard work and support under NAMASTE-SUY, Chetan has emerged as an inspiring example of sanitation entrepreneurship and self-reliance.

The assistance released on 14 September 2021 reflects the Government's commitment to promoting financial inclusion, improving livelihood opportunities and empowering sanitation workers through safe and sustainable entrepreneurship.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Launches the 5th Edition of ‘Swachh Sagar, Surakshit Sagar 2026’ as a Nationwide People’s Movement for Ocean Conservation
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:40PM by PIB Delhi

NEW DELHI, INDIA — Dr Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences, has officially launched the 5th edition of ‘Swachh Sagar, Surakshit Sagar 2026: SSSS v.5.0’. Building on its success over the last four years, the initiative has transformed into a powerful grassroots movement inspired by the Swachh Bharat vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Spearheaded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences, the campaign unites citizens, students, youth, coastal communities, and volunteer organisations/NGOs nationwide as part of Jan Bhagidhari to protect oceans and keep beaches pristine.

“Its “Swachh Sagar, Surakshit Sagar 5.0” from September 12 to 19, 2026. Let’s all come together for sea beach clean-up drives, Ocean pledge, youth activities, rallies and more, to protect India’s vast and precious coastal area. Take the pledge: https://niot.res.in/SSSS/pledge.php . Take the pledge. Be the change. Protect our oceans’’, he said through a post on X, at the SSSS v.5.0 launch.

In a Video message Dr. Jitendra Singh Said, ‘’today we are launching the fifth edition of Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar. Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar has been growing into a people's movement. India, as all of us know, has one of the longest stretches of coastal area spanning over 11,000 km and extending from the eastern to the western parts.’’

“Inspired by the vision of Deep Ocean Mission launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, the Ministry of Earth Sciences brings citizens, students, youth, coastal communities and organisations together to protect our oceans and keep our beaches clean. This year we want to take this movement to even greater scale. Swachh Sagar, Surakshat Sagar 5.0 will be a week-long celebration of our oceans from September 12 to September 19, 2026 with activities that bring people together from major beach clean-up drives and the ocean pledge to the Ocean Olympiad for our youth, cycling rallies, marathons, ozone day activities and many more programmes across the country’’, he added.

He said, “Dear friends, I especially urge you to take part in the Ocean Conservation Pledges by going into the Swachh Sagar Pledge website and take part in its India Coastal Cleanup event. Take this pledge with your family. Take this pledge with your friends. Take this pledge with all those around you. Encourage your school. Encourage your college. Encourage the organisation and community you are associated with to take it. Let this year's campaign become a massive Jan Bhagidari movement. Let us pledge to keep our shores clean, pledge to protect our oceans and pledge to build a healthier, cleaner, stronger India. So come forward, take the pledge and be a part of Swachh Sagar, Surakshat Sagar 5.0.”

Key Highlights of Swachh Sagar, Surakshit Sagar 5.0

  • Week-Long Celebration: Scheduled from September 12–19, 2026, featuring nationwide engagement activities.
  • Diverse Events: Major beach clean-up drives across 100+ locations, human chain, cycling rallies, marathons, and citizen engagement activities.
  • Youth Engagement: Launch of the first-ever national Ocean Olympiad to foster environmental awareness among students and youth.
  • Digital Launches: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh unveiled a dedicated official pledge on ocean conservation, the SSSS v.5.0 website, an introductory video, and a video on activities schedules as part of the SSSS v.5.0.

 

Mark Your Contribution

The Ministry invites all citizens to mark their presence in India’s marquee coastal cleanup event through the following official platforms:

 

  • Contribute to engaging activities for ocean conservation, participate in beach clean-up: Log on to the Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar website https://niot.res.in/SSSS/ for details on beach locations and a brochure.
  • Take the Ocean Pledge: Commitment to ocean conservation. https://niot.res.in/SSSS/pledge.php
  • Download the SAGAR PRAHARI App: Stay connected by downloading the SSSS v.5.0 mobile app available at   

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.swachhsagar.release&hl=en_IN

  • Participate in the Ocean Olympiad: Citizens can register and test their knowledge via the Ocean Olympiad https://www.oceanolympiad.com/

item.content:encoded:
UPSC
Combined Medical Services Examination 2026
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:27PM by PIB Delhi

On the basis of the result of the written part of the Combined Medical Services Examination 2026 held by the UPSC on 2nd August, 2026, the candidates with the under mentioned Roll Numbers have qualified for Interview/Personality Test.

2. The candidature of these candidates is PROVISIONAL subject to their being found eligible in all respects. The candidates would be required to produce the original certificates in support of their claims relating to age, educational qualifications, community, benchmark disability (where applicable) etc. at the time of the Personality Test. They are, therefore, advised to keep their certificates ready and check beforehand the requirement of certificates in accordance with the important instructions available on the website of the Commission before appearing in the Personality Test.

3.1 The Commission shall provide a window of 15 (Fifteen) days after the declaration of written result of Combined Medical Services (CMS) Examination, 2026. All the candidates, as per Rule 9(a)(ii) of Rules of CMS Examination, 2026, who qualified for the Personality Test/Interview shall be required to mandatorily login to the portal (https://upsconline.nic.in) during this period and shall be required to update their details/educational qualification status (whether appearing/appeared) alongwith proof of passing the requisite qualifying examination, and upload the relevant documents as proof of their claim, failing which, such candidates will not be allowed to participate in the further stages of this examination and no correspondence will be entertained by the Commission in this regard.

3.2 In this period, all the candidates, who qualified for Personality Test shall also be provided an option to update the Correspondence/ Permanent Postal Address, Higher Educational Qualification, Achievement in different fields (if any), Employment Details/Service Experience, details of the Service allocated on the basis of earlier/previous Combined Medical Services Examination (if any), Marital Status, PwBD Recommendation details in past, Parental Details, Debarment information, earlier Examination details, OBC/EWS Annexure (wherever applicable) and submit their Online Application Form.

3.3 Candidates who have uploaded the required documents/information earlier and have no information to update/fill in, are also required to mandatorily login and finally submit after verifying the details so as to generate the e-summon letter for Personality Test/Interview of CMS Examination-2026. The candidates are advised to regularly visit the Commission’s website with regard to further updates

4. The instruction for updating the Application Form and Rules of the Combined Medical Services Examination, 2026, must be read carefully with regard to the certificates that will be produced at the time of Interview. The candidates will be solely responsible for not producing sufficient proof in support of his/her age, date of birth, educational qualification, community (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) and physical disability certificate (in the case of PwBD candidates). In case any of the written qualified candidate fails to bring any or all the required original documents in support of his/her candidature for the Combined Medical Services Examination, 2026, he/she will not be allowed to present himself/herself before the PT Board and no TA will be allowed.

5. The Schedule of the Interview of candidates, who have qualified for the Personality Test, will be uploaded on the Commission’s website in due course of time. The exact date of interview will, however, be intimated to the candidates through e-Summon Letter. The candidates are requested to visit the Commission’s website (https://upsc.gov.in) for updates in this regard.

6. No request for change in the date and time of Personality Test intimated to the candidates will ordinarily be entertained under any circumstances.

7. The mark-sheet of candidates will be uploaded on the Commission's website after the publication of final result (i.e. after conducting Personality Test) and will remain available on the website for a period of 30 days.

8. The candidates can access the marks-sheets after keying in their Roll Numbers and date of birth. The printed/hard copies of the marks-sheet would, however, be issued by the UPSC to candidates based on specific request accompanied by a self-addressed stamped envelope. Candidates desirous of obtaining printed/hard copies of the marks sheets should make the request within 30 days of the display of the marks on the Commission's website, beyond which such requests would not be entertained.

9. The candidates may obtain any information/clarification regarding their issue(s) (if any) in respect of the above mentioned Examination on Tel. No. 011-40303444/24041001 of the Commission’s Call Centre from 09:00 AM to 08:00 PM.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Ministry of Education extends deadline for NMMSS 2026-27 scholarship applications to  September 30, 2026
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

The last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 has been extended to September 30, 2026. The extended timeline is as follows:

 

Particulars

Extended timelines

Last date for Submission of Application

30.09.2026

Last date for INO verification (L1)

15.10.2026

Last date for DNO verification (L2)

31.10.2026

 

The NSP portal is open for submission of applications by students with effect from June 1, 2026. In this project year, that is, 2026-27, selected students have to do a one-time registration (OTR) on the NSP, after which they have to apply for the scholarship scheme that they have selected.

The ‘National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme’, implemented by the Department of School Education & Literacy, Union Ministry of Education, awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level, i.e., Class VIII and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level, i.e., Class XII.

The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class IX students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State/UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes X to XII based on the student's academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools. The scholarship amount is Rs. 12,000 per annum per student.

NMMSS scholarships are disbursed directly into the bank accounts of selected students by electronic transfer through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) following DBT mode. The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than Rs. 3.50 lakh per annum, a minimum of 55% marks or equivalent grade in the Class VII examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship (relaxable by 5% for SC/ST students).

The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) - the one-stop platform for scholarship schemes disbursed to students by the Government of India. As of 31.08.2026, 79,398 fresh and 1,87, 208 renewal applications have been submitted.

All eligible students are advised to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) within the extended timeline. Students who have already submitted their applications should also ensure that their applications are duly verified by the concerned Institute/District/State Nodal Officers, as applicable.

 

On the NSP portal, there are two levels of verification of the scholarship application of selected students, Level-1 (L1) verification is at the Institute Nodal Officer (INO) and Level-2 (L2) is with the District Nodal Officer (DNO). The last date for INO level (L1) verification is 15.10.2026 and for DNO level (L2) verification is 31.10.2026.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
“Rajdharma Is a Continuing Ethic of Public Office”: Arif Mohammed Khan addresses EPFO Officers, Calls for Integrity, Empathy and Non-Discrimination in Governance
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:14PM by PIB Delhi

In a thought-provoking keynote at Reimagining Governance: Discourse for Excellence (RGDE), Shri Arif Mohammed Khan called for a deeper understanding of Rajdharma as an enduring ethic of public responsibility, emphasising integrity, empathy, fairness and non-discrimination in the exercise of public authority.

The session was organised by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) on 31st August 2026, under the aegis of the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security (PDUNASS), as part of the second edition of Season Two of RGDE. Senior officers and officials from EPFO and PDUNASS, along with officers from Field offices of EPFO joining virtually from across the country, participated in the session.

Rajdharma and the Responsibility of Public Power

Shri Khan reflected on the continuity and distinctiveness of Indian civilisation and described Dharma as a principle of righteous conduct and moral obligation. He emphasised that Rajdharma is ultimately concerned with the responsibility of those entrusted with public power and with the manner in which that power is exercised. He underlined the importance of non-discrimination in public life and of cultivating an approach in which the official seeks to serve rather than merely exercise authority.

He connected this ethical foundation with the inner discipline expected of a person holding public office. Referring to the spiritual idea that the Divine is present in every human being, Shri Khan stressed that an officer’s conduct should be guided by sincerity, honesty, self-restraint and a consciousness that public responsibility carries a moral dimension beyond formal procedure.

Reflecting on governance in practical terms, he stressed that rules, systems and technology are important instruments, but they cannot substitute for the human qualities that ultimately determine how citizens experience an institution. He emphasised that sincerity, cultural awareness and ethical conduct must remain at the heart of administration, particularly when officials are called upon to exercise judgement in everyday situations.

Rajdharma in the Context of Social Security

Central Provident Fund Commissioner Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi contextualised the discussion within EPFO’s responsibility for providing social security to millions of workers, pensioners and their families. He emphasised the importance of balancing legal compliance with empathy and citizen-centric service delivery as the organisation embraces technological transformation.

He highlighted the need for officers to approach their responsibilities with a spirit of selfless service, particularly while dealing with the real-life circumstances behind claims, pensions and grievances.

Civilisational Wisdom and Contemporary Governance

Director, PDUNASS, Shri Kumar Rohit, highlighted the enduring relevance of Rajdharma to contemporary public administration. Referring to the Bharat-Milap episode at Chitrakoot, he recalled how Lord Rama, while declining to return to Ayodhya, entrusted Bharata with the responsibility of governance through his Charan Padukas and imparted timeless counsel on righteous statecraft.

He emphasised that RGDE seeks to create a space where civilisational wisdom, institutional experience and contemporary administrative practice can inform one another, ultimately returning to the central purpose of public service: serving the citizen with fairness, dignity and responsibility.

Ideas to Institutional Practice

The session also featured an interactive exchange with officers, focusing on the practical application of ethical and civilisational values in everyday administration, including situations where officials must exercise judgement, balance rules with circumstances, and retain empathy while working in increasingly technology-enabled systems.

The session was moderated by Shri Prashant Sharma, RPFC-I, who facilitated the proceedings and the interaction with Shri Khan, connecting the philosophical idea of Rajdharma with the practical realities of public service.

The session concluded with expressions of gratitude to Shri Arif Mohammed Khan and the participating officers, reaffirming PDUNASS’s commitment to fostering a culture of learning, reflection and excellence in public service.

***

Rini Choudhury/Anjelina Alexander

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri conducts annual performance review of 16 DPSUs; Lauds their noteworthy contribution in record defence production
Shri Rajnath Singh urges DPSUs to focus on timely delivery, self-reliance, exports & global-standard quality
“In pursuit of ‘Make in India, Make for the World’, we must transform DPSUs into global giants”
Progress of DPSUs is not merely an economic or industrial necessity; it is a national security imperative: RM
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh reviewed the annual performance of 16 Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) in New Delhi on September 01, 2026. During the meeting, Raksha Mantri, along with Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, was briefed by Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar and the Chairmen & Managing Directors (CMDs) of the DPSUs on their performance, key achievements, and future roadmap. Raksha Mantri reviewed the progress made by the DPSUs in enhancing indigenous production and manufacturing capabilities, development of advanced defence technologies, increasing defence exports, strengthening supply chains and execution of major projects.

In his address, Raksha Mantri commended the DPSUs for their steadfast contribution to strengthening India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem and advancing the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat while building a robust defence industrial base ecosystem. He stated that all the 16 DPSUs are showing their achievement in multi sectors and congratulated the organizations for their continued dedication and excellence. He underlined that in the year 2025-26, India achieved defence production worth approx. Rs 1.8 lakh crore with DPSUs contributing Rs. 1.29 lakh crore. He termed the achievement a reflection of the nation’s significant progress towards building an Aatmanirbhar defence industrial base.

Shri Rajnath Singh urged the DPSUs to focus on timely delivery, reducing the import dependency, transforming R&D into technology leadership, enhancing defence exports to newer heights, increasing productivity with their capex expansion, supporting start-ups & MSMEs further and making efforts to achieve quality equivalent to global standards. “The progress of DPSUs is not merely an economic or industrial necessity; it is a national security imperative. Recent global conflicts have demonstrated how crucial assured supply chains, surge capacity, critical spares, rapid repair capabilities, and the ability to sustain production during prolonged conflicts are for any nation,” he said.

While Raksha Mantri welcomed the increased investment in R&D by DPSUs, he stated that the success of R&D should be measured not just by the amount spent, but by the development of new technologies, intellectual property, prototypes, and operational products. “We must identify niche technology areas where India can become not just self-reliant, but a global leader,” he said.

Raksha Mantri urged the DPSUs to continue focusing on elevating the quality of their products to global standards. “In pursuit of the ‘Make in India, Make for the World’ objective, we must resolve to transform all DPSUs into global giants,” he said.

During the event, the CMDs of seven DPSUs - Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE), BEML, and MIDHANI - presented dividend cheques, worth a total of Rs 3,951 crore for the Government's equity shares to the Raksha Mantri for FY 2025-26.

On the occasion, Raksha Mantri released four books namely ‘Aatmanirbhar DPSU - A journey of DPSUs towards Self-Reliance’ on indigenisation of items, new products to be developed and new processes to be adopted for the next five years; DISHA, an initiative for industries’ interaction with students for the young minds’ hands-on awareness on defence technologies & modern manufacturing processes; Modernisation Roadmap of HAL to transform it into a future-ready aerospace enterprise; and Indigenisation Roadmap of HAL to achieve greater self-reliance in aero & defence sector. The publications highlight the efforts towards self-reliance, indigenisation, innovation and building future-ready defence capabilities.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
AIIA Launches ‘AyurVarta’ Digital Dialogue Series Ahead of Ayurveda Day
First Episode Highlights Significance of 23rd September as Fixed Date for Ayurveda Day
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Ayush, has launched ‘AyurVarta’, a special digital dialogue series aimed at taking authentic knowledge, scientific perspectives and contemporary relevance of Ayurveda to wider audiences in India and abroad.

The initiative has been launched ahead of Ayurveda Day, which will be observed on 23 September. The series will feature conversations with leading experts on Ayurveda, contemporary healthcare challenges, scientific research, education, clinical practice and the growing global relevance of Ayurveda.

The inaugural episode of ‘AyurVarta’ featured a discussion between Professor (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, and Professor (Dr.) Mahesh Vyas, Dean, Ph.D., AIIA, on the theme “Why is Ayurveda Day celebrated on 23 September?”

The discussion traced the evolution of Ayurveda Day, which was earlier observed on Dhanvantari Jayanti (Dhanteras), and highlighted the Government’s decision to designate 23 September as the fixed date for its annual observance.

Speaking on the occasion, Professor (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, sustained efforts are being made to strengthen Ayurveda as an important knowledge and healthcare system with growing relevance in the global health landscape.

He said that the observance of Ayurveda Day on a fixed date will provide greater consistency and a stronger national and international identity to the annual celebration.

Prof. Prajapati further stated that ‘AyurVarta’ is a digital extension of this vision and will provide audiences with access to authentic knowledge and expert perspectives on Ayurveda.

During the discussion, Professor (Dr.) Mahesh Vyas, highlighted the significance associated with 23 September, which falls around the Autumnal Equinox, when the duration of day and night is approximately equal.

He explained that the idea of balance and equilibrium is central to the Ayurvedic understanding of health and well-being. In this context, the date also provides a conceptual association with Ayurveda’s emphasis on balance, harmony and equilibrium.

‘AyurVarta’ has been conceived as a continuing digital initiative to facilitate informed dialogue on various dimensions of Ayurveda. The series will bring together Ayurveda experts, physicians, academicians, scientists, researchers and policy experts from India and abroad.

Future episodes of ‘AyurVarta’ will explore a wide range of subjects, including:

  • Scientific foundations of Ayurveda and contemporary research
  • Ayurveda education and the role of the younger generation
  • Ayurveda and public health
  • Innovation and technology in Ayurveda
  • Integration of Ayurveda with modern medical sciences
  • Medicinal plants and natural resources
  • Healthy lifestyles and preventive healthcare
  • Ayurveda and global health
  • International opportunities and expansion of Ayurveda
  • Research, evidence generation and evidence-based Ayurveda

Episodes of ‘AyurVarta’ will be disseminated through AIIA’s official digital and social media platforms, including YouTube, Facebook, X and Instagram, enabling access for students, young people, physicians, researchers, academicians and the general public.

The first episode of ‘AyurVarta’ is available at the following YouTube link:- Watch ‘AyurVarta’ – First Episode on YouTube

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Swachhata Pakhwada-2026 Begins in Department of Fertilizers with Message from Union Minister Shri J. P. Nadda
Officials and Employees of the Department Take Swachhata Pledge Under the Leadership of Secretary, Shri Rajat Kumar Mishra
Department Officials and Employees Reaffirm Their Commitment to Cleanliness and a Clean Work Culture
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

Swachhata Pakhwada-2026 commenced in the Department of Fertilizers, Government of India, with a message from the Hon’ble Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri J. P. Nadda. In his message, the Hon’ble Minister described Swachhata Pakhwada as an important nationwide initiative towards building a clean, green and sustainable India.

In his message, the Hon’ble Minister said, “Swachhata Pakhwada is a nationwide initiative that reflects our vision of a clean, green and sustainable India and strengthens our collective commitment to maintaining clean and healthy workplaces and surrounding environments, in line with the objectives of Swachh Bharat.”

He called upon all officers and employees to actively participate in the cleanliness campaign and contribute towards making its observance successful and meaningful. He also extended his best wishes for the successful conduct of Swachhata Pakhwada-2026.

Following the Hon’ble Minister’s message, officials and employees of the Department of Fertilizers took the Swachhata Pledge under the leadership of Shri Rajat Kumar Mishra, Secretary, Department of Fertilizers, Government of India.

On the occasion, the Secretary called upon all officers and employees to extend active cooperation towards the cleanliness initiative. He stated that cleanliness is not merely a campaign but a moral responsibility and it is the responsibility of every individual to uphold it. He urged everyone to maintain cleanliness at their workplace and in the surrounding environment and to make cleanliness an integral part of their daily work culture.

The officials and employees of the Department participated enthusiastically in the Swachhata Pledge programme and resolved to discharge their responsibilities towards cleanliness with sincerity and dedication. They also expressed their commitment to creating a clean and healthy office environment, enhancing awareness about cleanliness and keeping their workplaces neat and clean.

The Department of Fertilizers is observing Swachhata Pakhwada-2026 from 1st to 15th September 2026. During the Pakhwada, various activities are being organised to promote cleanliness, environmental protection, digital cleanliness and a clean work culture.

स्वच्छ, हरित, पेपरलेस और डिजिटल रूप से सशक्त कार्य-परिवेश का निर्माण हमारा संकल्प है.

'स्वच्छता पखवाड़ा 2026' की शुरुआत करते हुए आज श्री रजत कुमार मिश्रा, सचिव उर्वरक विभाग ने विभाग के अधिकारियों और कर्मचारियों को स्वच्छता की शपथ दिलाई#SwachhBharat pic.twitter.com/DlYtWbcDjE

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
AVM SHAKTI SHARMA SCRIPTS HISTORY AS FIRST (NON-MEDICAL) WOMAN TWO-STAR OFFICER IN THE DEFENCE SERVICES
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 6:01PM by PIB Delhi

In a historic milestone for the Indian Air Force Air Vice Marshal Shakti Sharma  became the first woman officer (non-medical) in the Indian Defence Forces to attain the rank of Air Vice Marshal (or equivalent). On 01 September 2026, she assumed the appointment of Assistant Chief of the Air Staff (Education) at Air Headquarters.

Commissioned into the Education Branch of the IAF on 18 June 1994, AVM Shakti Sharma brings a wealth of experience to her new role, spanning diverse postings across Training Establishments, Field Stations, Command Headquarters, and Air Headquarters. Throughout her career, she has spearheaded key institutional initiatives, including establishing the IAF Chairs of Excellence at IlT Kanpur and Pune University to drive academic and strategic defense collaboration. She also created history as the first woman officer from the Tri-Services to command a Sainik School, serving as Principal of Sainik School, Kapurthala.

This landmark achievemenț marks a new chapter in the journey of women officers in the Indian Defence Forces. With over three decades of distinguished service, she continues to inspire generations to “Touch the Sky with Glory”.

L. Verma Twenty Stalls Showcase The Traditional Crafts And Products Of DNT Artisans From Six States And UTs Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi The Development and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
More than 700 Beneficiaries Participate in ‘SAMAVESH UTSAV’ Celebrating Inclusion, Empowerment and Progress of DNT Communities
The SEED Scheme Is Helping In Transforming Lives Through Interventions In Education, Healthcare, Livelihood And Housing: Dr Virendra Kumar
The SEED Scheme Is Reliably Improving The Socio-Economic Conditions Of DNT Communities: Shri B. L. Verma
Twenty Stalls Showcase The Traditional Crafts And Products Of DNT Artisans From Six States And UTs
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC), under the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, organised ‘SAMAVESH UTSAV’ at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre in National Capital today.

More than 700 beneficiaries from De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic (DNT) communities including community leaders and artisans from across the country, participated in the programme.

The event celebrated the inclusion, empowerment and progress of DNT communities by showcasing success stories under the Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs (SEED). It also highlighted the traditional skills, craftsmanship and products of DNT artisans, along with various initiatives undertaken by the Government for the welfare of these communities.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar shared experiences from his interactions with DNT communities across the country. He appreciated the positive impact of the SEED Scheme in transforming their lives, particularly through interventions in education, healthcare, livelihood and housing.

The Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma, senior representatives of the Ministry and DWBDNC including CEO Board Shri Rajan Sehgal, Members Shri Bharatbhai Babubhai Patni and Shri Pravin Shivajirao Ghuge, also graced the occasion.

Shri B. L. Verma highlighted the role of the SEED Scheme in improving the socio-economic conditions of DNT communities. He reiterated the Government’s continued commitment to their holistic welfare, empowerment and inclusion.

 

A major attraction of SAMAVESH UTSAV was an exhibition showcasing the traditional skills and products of DNT artisans. Twenty stalls featured artisans from Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Delhi, representing communities such as Banjara, Chamar, Nat, Sutar, Vadar, Lohar, Gadiya Lohar, Waghri and Naik.

The products displayed at the exhibition included handmade godhadis, jute bags, traditional jhulas, hand embroidery, blue pottery, iron products, appliqué and block-print work, pickles, spices and fruit jams. The exhibition offered visitors a glimpse into the rich craft heritage, creativity and entrepreneurial potential of DNT communities.

The Government constituted the DWBDNC through a notification dated 21st February 2019 to implement welfare and development programmes for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic communities. The SEED Scheme was subsequently launched to supplement efforts aimed at their holistic welfare and socio-economic empowerment.

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sexual assault of a minor girl by a bus driver and conductor in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh
Issues notices to Police Commissioners of Delhi and Gautam Budh Nagar and Mainpuri Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the victim
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a 16-year-old girl was subjected to gang rape by a driver and a conductor of a bus that she boarded from Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh on 4th August 2026. Reportedly, the perpetrators extended life threats and left her at the Kashmere Gate Bus Terminal in Delhi.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of human rights violations. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Police Commissioners of Delhi and Gautam Budh Nagar and Mainpuri Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the victim.

According to the media report, carried on 31st August 2026, the girl left home in Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh to visit her cousin in Sector 63, but she missed her stop and alighted at Pari Chowk. From there, she reportedly boarded another bus after confirming that it was going to Sector 63 of Noida.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Education
item.description: Ministry of Education Union Minister for Education graces NCERT’s 66th Foundation Day celebrations in New Delhi Let us make NCERT more innovative, inclusive, research-driven and future-ready - Shri Pralhad Joshi NCERT has a vital role in transforming school education and shaping the future of our children - Union Education Minister Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 5:35PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi today noted that NCERT has played an important role in the Indian education system for more than six decades, particularly through its textbooks,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Union Minister for Education graces NCERT’s 66th Foundation Day celebrations in New Delhi
Let us make NCERT more innovative, inclusive, research-driven and future-ready - Shri Pralhad Joshi
NCERT has a vital role in transforming school education and shaping the future of our children - Union Education Minister
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 5:35PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi today noted that NCERT has played an important role in the Indian education system for more than six decades, particularly through its textbooks, learning materials, and curriculum frameworks. The Minister was speaking at the 66th Foundation Day celebrations of NCERT at its headquarters in New Delhi

The Union Minister said that the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 provided a framework for reforms in school education, with emphasis on holistic development, creativity, critical thinking, experiential learning and competency-based education. In this context, he highlighted NCERT’s work on the National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS) 2022, the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE) 2023, and the development of new textbooks for Grades 1 to 9. Appreciating NCERT’s efforts towards multilingual education, the Minister informed that textbooks for Grades 1 to 8 were being prepared in all 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, along with 121 primers in different Indian languages, including 93 tribal languages. He added that the new textbooks were making learning more engaging and relevant while remaining rooted in India’s heritage, with Indian Knowledge Systems integrated across the textbooks.

Shri Joshi also emphasised the need for NCERT to continue strengthening its research ecosystem and use of technology, particularly in view of the growing role of Artificial Intelligence in education and society. He noted the importance of equipping learners with digital literacy, AI awareness, critical thinking, problem-solving and innovation skills, while also giving due attention to the mental well-being of students through appropriate curricular interventions, psychosocial support and teacher training.

Highlighting the launch of the Robotics Learning Centre, Translation Lab, and the upgraded Television Studio, he said that these facilities would support technology-enabled learning, education in Indian languages, and the development of educational content. He added that the next phase of NCERT’s development should build on its existing institutional experience while responding to emerging educational needs.

In addition to the Robotics and the Translation Labs and the upgraded TV studio, the Union Minister also inaugurated the newly constructed Gate No. 2 complex and a theme park. The occasion also featured the release of the Coffee Table Book, titled, Flora and Fauna at NCERT.

Shri Joshi also visited the exhibition organised as part of the celebrations showcasing NCERT’s initiatives across various domains, including curriculum framework development, Jaadui Pitara, and digital education platforms such as PM eVIDYA, DIKSHA and eJaadui Pitara.

Chairman, Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti, Dr. Chamu Krishna Shastry; Director, NCERT, Prof. Dinesh Prasad Saklani, and senior officials of the Ministry of Education and NCERT were present on the occasion.

Summit to focus on four key areas covering Timely implementation of Water Infrastructure Projects, Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari, Drinking Water Source Sustainability and Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 5:08PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will participate in the valedictory session Departmental Summit of Ministry of Jal Shakti on 2nd September 2026 at around 4:30 PM at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

The two-day Departmental Summit, being held on 1-2 September 2026, is the first in a series of Departmental Summits envisioned by Prime Minister to strengthen the spirit of Team India, deepen cooperative federalism and foster collective ownership of national priorities through closer collaboration between the Centre and the States. The initiative provides a structured platform to jointly deliberate on critical sectoral priorities and accelerate implementation and outcomes.

The Summit will bring together political leadership and senior officials from the Union and State Governments to deliberate on key priorities, share best practices, address implementation challenges and evolve time-bound action plans. The initiative seeks to promote shared responsibility for national goals and ensure that deliberations translate into measurable improvements in governance and service delivery.

The Summit will focus on four key areas:

  1. Timely implementation of water infrastructure projects
  2. Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari - Catch the Rain
  3. Source sustainability of drinking water systems
  4. Operation and maintenance of rural drinking water supply schemes under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0

The consultations are expected to result in concrete and time-bound actions for accelerating water infrastructure projects, enhancing public participation in water conservation, ensuring sustainable drinking water sources and improving the reliability and accountability of rural drinking water services.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Rajya Mantri Delivers Special Address at Second Annual Trident Lecture of CENJOWS
“India Must Prepare for the Wars of the Future Through Innovation, Self-Reliance and Civil-Military Fusion” : RRM
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 5:05PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth attended the Second Annual ‘Trident Lecture’ orga­nized by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS) at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi on September 01, 2026 and delivered a Special Address on the theme ‘Leveraging the Po­tential of Next Generation for Nation Building’.

During his address, the Raksha Rajya Mantri underscored the significance of jointness, in­tegration, civil-military coordination and a strong and self-reliant defence system in the con­text of the evolving global security environment. Shri Seth highlighted that, under the guid­ance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the leadership of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh, India is continuously strengthening its defence capabilities and progressing towards the vision of aatmanirbhar and developed India. He stated that the commitment of the Defence Forces, adoption of modern technology and enhanced coordination among the three Services are the foundation of a strong and secure India.

Highlighting the strength of India’s youth, Shri Seth said that the young population is contribut­ing across a wide range of sectors, including defence, industry, startups, space, agriculture,

technology and sports. He noted that India’s aspiration has evolved from “Make in India” to “Make for the World”, reflecting the country’s transition from import dependence towards man­ufacturing and export of globally competitive products and technologies.

Applauding the growing role of Indian MSMEs and indigenous industries, RRM stressed the need to strengthen national capabilities in semiconductors, electronics and advanced tech­nologies to prepare for the wars of the future.

Addressing the gathering, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, CISC, noted that national security now encompasses economic security, technological competition, maritime resilience, critical in­frastructure, supply chains and information integrity, in addition to territorial defence. Refer­ring to recent operational experience, including Operation Sindoor, he underlined the impor­tance of coordinated planning and integrated execution.

Other eminent speakers including Vice Chief of the Army Staff Lt Gen Sandeep Jain and Lt Gen Raj Shukla (Retd) deliberated on significant topics like civil military fusion, Multi domain warfare, emerging technologies, jointness and India's preparedness for future security challenges. The discussions reinforced the need for a forward-looking, integrated and innovation-driven approach to national security as India advances towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

During the event, RRM also launched the book titled " An Era in Olive Green: Gen Anil Chauhan, Duty, Leadership and Legacy".

The 2nd Annual Trident Lecture concluded with the closing address by Vice Admiral Rajesh Dhankhar, Deputy Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (Doctrine, Organisation and Training).

VK/Ruchi

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja takes over as DGAFMS
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi

Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja assumed the appointment of the 47th Director General Armed Forces Medical Services (DGAFMS) on September 01, 2026. As the DGAFMS, Air Marshal Thareja will oversee the provision of comprehensive medical support to the Defence Forces. His appointment comes at a time of significant transformation within the AFMS, with continuing emphasis on operational medical preparedness, jointness, modernisation of military healthcare, digital health, medical research and innovation, human-resource development and delivery of high-quality healthcare to serving personnel, veterans and their dependents.

An alumnus of the Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC), Pune, Air Marshal Thareja was commissioned into the Army Medical Corps in December 1986. A distinguished physician and gastroenterologist, he completed his MD in Medicine from Delhi and DM in Gastroenterology from AIIMS, New Delhi.

During an illustrious career spanning nearly four decades, the Air Marshal has held a wide spectrum of clinical, academic, operational and administrative appointments. His important command and administrative assignments include Commandant, 167 Military Hospital, Brigadier In-Charge Administration and Commander Troops, Base Hospital Delhi Cantt and Commandant Command Hospital (Central Command). His tenure at Base Hospital Delhi Cantt during the COVID-19 pandemic was marked by the management of complex and rapidly evolving healthcare and administrative challenges. During his command of Command Hospital, Lucknow the Detailed Project Report for a new Command Hospital was prepared in record time.

As Director and Commandant at AFMC Pune, he spearheaded several initiatives aimed at strengthening medical education and research. As DGMS (Air) he gave thrust to Gaganyaan Mission and was the leading force behind Analog experiments to Astronaut Selection & Training. BHISHM (Bharat Health Initiative for Sahyog Hita & Maitri) cubes were gifted to the Maldives by the Prime Minister and as part of HADR to Jamaica, Cuba, Sri Lanka & Myanmar under his stewardship.

Prior to taking over as DG AFMS, Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja laid a wreath at the National War Memorial, New Delhi paid homage to the fallen heroes.

******

VK/Savvy

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
CARA Launches Adoption Awareness 2026 Theme to Promote Legal Adoption and Say No to Illegal Adoption
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 4:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA), under the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, has launched the theme for Adoption Awareness 2026, reinforcing its commitment to promoting legal, safe, transparent and child-centric adoption across the country.

The theme for Adoption Awareness 2026 is:

Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future.

Say No to Illegal Adoption!

The theme was formally launched by Smt. Bhavna Saxena, CEO, CARA, during a Live Morning Show on DD National, marking the beginning of a sustained nationwide awareness initiative to promote legal adoption and prevent illegal adoption practices.

During the programme, Smt. Bhavna Saxena, CEO, CARA, emphasised the importance of following the legal adoption process and said, “Adoption is not a shortcut—it is a sacred responsibility. Through CARA and the legally prescribed channels, we safeguard the dignity, rights and future of every orphaned, abandoned or surrendered child. Every child deserves a safe, loving and secure family—not secrecy, uncertainty or risk.”

CARA has been undertaking several measures to strengthen awareness, coordination and enforcement against illegal adoption practices, including enhanced coordination with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Ministry of Home Affairs. However, sustained awareness and capacity building at the State, district and community levels remain critical to ensuring that every child is protected and every adoption is carried out through the prescribed legal process.

Year-Round Outreach to Promote Legal Adoption

Under the theme “Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future. Say No to Illegal Adoption,” several outreach activities will be conducted throughout the year to create widespread awareness among citizens and key stakeholders.

As part of the initiative, State/UT-level Adoption Awareness Workshops are being organised from September 2026 onwards, moving beyond the earlier approach of limiting adoption awareness activities to the month of November. These workshops will provide a platform for stakeholders to understand the statutory adoption process, strengthen inter-departmental coordination, identify and address illegal adoption practices, and reinforce the principle of the best interest of the child.

The campaign will involve a wide range of stakeholders, including Women and Child Development Departments, Child Welfare Committees, District Child Protection Units, Specialised Adoption Agencies, Child Care Institutions, Police, Health Departments, Judiciary, Legal Services Authorities, hospitals and nursing homes, medical professionals, ASHA and ANM workers, civil society organisations, media and digital platforms, among others.

Adoption Awareness Workshop in Delhi on 10 September 2026

As part of this nationwide initiative, CARA will organise an Adoption Awareness Workshop in Delhi on Thursday, 10 September 2026, at the Delhi Secretariat, New Delhi in collaboration of Department of Women and Child Development, Govt. of Delhi and concerned authorities.

The workshop will focus on strengthening awareness regarding the legal adoption framework and the roles and responsibilities of stakeholders in ensuring that children in need of care and protection receive appropriate care, protection and rehabilitation through lawful mechanisms.

The workshop will also emphasise the importance of timely reporting of children found separated from their guardians, lawful surrender procedures, declaration of children as legally free for adoption, and adherence to the prescribed adoption procedure.

A Collective Responsibility to Protect Every Child

The campaign seeks to ensure that prospective adoptive parents and the general public understand that adoption is a legal and child-centric process—not a private arrangement between individuals.

Citizens are encouraged to follow only the legally prescribed adoption process through CARA and the designated authorities/agencies and to report suspected instances of illegal adoption to the competent authorities.

Through sustained, year-round awareness and coordinated action, CARA aims to build a stronger ecosystem in which every child’s dignity, identity, rights, safety and future are protected.

***

SS/PC

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh Calls for Wider Awareness about Rs 1 Lakh Crore RDI Fund Among Stakeholders to Ensure Right Beneficiaries Avail of Support Greater Outreach Needed to Ensure RDI Fund Reaches Technology and Research Stakeholders and Contributes to National Economic Growth Technology Development Board Must Evolve as a Strategic Enabler of India’s Future Technology Sectors: Dr. Jitendra Singh Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 4:35PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh today called for greater awareness and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Dr. Jitendra Singh Calls for Wider Awareness about Rs 1 Lakh Crore RDI Fund Among Stakeholders to Ensure Right Beneficiaries Avail of Support
Greater Outreach Needed to Ensure RDI Fund Reaches Technology and Research Stakeholders and Contributes to National Economic Growth
Technology Development Board Must Evolve as a Strategic Enabler of India’s Future Technology Sectors: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 4:35PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh today called for greater awareness and outreach about Rs 1 Lakh Crore “Research, Development and Innovation Fund” (RDI Fund) among stakeholders so that the right kind of applicants understand its purpose, eligibility and the process for availing support.

Addressing the 30th Foundation Day of the Technology Development Board (TDB), Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the focus should be on creating awareness about the spirit behind the RDI Fund, the stakeholders and companies eligible for support, and how they can avail of the funding. He observed that the large number of applications being received also indicated a need for greater clarity and outreach about the purpose of the Fund.

The Minister said that thousands of applications are being received, including from applicants who do not appear to understand the nature and purpose of the RDI Fund. He cautioned against the perception that the Fund is simply another source of finance or a conventional loan facility, stressing the need to ensure that there is no misunderstanding about the funding process.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the RDI Fund is intended to support technology development and research in a manner that contributes to the progress of science and research and makes these activities part of the overall growth of the national economy. He called for efforts to ensure that stakeholders understand the spirit and intended purpose of the Fund so that its benefits reach the appropriate beneficiaries.

The Minister emphasised that the funding process is already transparent and has proper safeguards in place, even though the government is open to suggestions for further safeguards wherever feasible. He said, there is scope to further increase outreach and awareness. He said that better awareness would help the right kind of people avail of the support in the interest of scientific and research progress and its contribution to national economic growth.

Referring to the role of TDB, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Board must also play a role in educating those for whom such initiatives are meant. He stressed that while technology and policy frameworks are changing rapidly, the mindset of stakeholders also needs to change accordingly.

The Minister said that TDB was created with the vision of ensuring that technologies do not remain confined to laboratories but are translated into products, solutions and enterprises that can bring ease of living to citizens, provide livelihoods and contribute to the overall economy of the country. He said that the occasion of the 30th Foundation Day was an opportunity to look back at how far this spirit had been carried forward.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that over the last 12 years this spirit had been vindicated and credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with placing science, technology and innovation high on the government agenda. He described the period as a decade of scientific renaissance in the country, highlighting achievements in science and technology and India's ability to deliver cost-effective successes.

Emphasising the importance of changing mindsets, the Minister said that continuous learning and curiosity would be essential to keeping pace with rapid technological developments. He stressed that stakeholders must make the best use of the enabling environment provided by policymakers.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the growth of the start-up ecosystem and called for prevailing myths about entrepreneurship to be dispelled. He noted that start-ups are not confined to Bengaluru or Hyderabad, that more than 50 per cent are from smaller towns, and that entrepreneurship is not necessarily restricted to young people. He also highlighted the participation of women in the ecosystem.

The Minister underlined the importance of openness to private-sector participation and said that this approach had been followed in sectors including space, biotechnology and the nuclear sector. He stressed that resource pooling and integration among institutions and stakeholders are important for strengthening the ecosystem.

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated TDB's role in supporting the journey from laboratory to market and noted that the Board had, in practice, extended support beyond narrowly defined domains. He referred to examples including Skyroot and BotLab, and said that moving beyond a conventional bureaucratic approach had enabled TDB to become an important part of the emerging technology ecosystem.

The Minister also highlighted the need for a culture of philanthropy in research. He said that funding research that ultimately contributes to the well-being of mankind should also be recognised as a form of worship and called for such a culture to be created.

Looking ahead, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that TDB should support technology development both in the early phase and at the later stage. He noted that the RDI Fund is offering support at a later stage at TRL4 level and that TDB is the first to roll out its proposals.

He said that TDB has set up a model of public-private transition and technology self-reliance which could become an important pillar of India's economy and contribute not only to India but also to the Global South. He further observed that strengthening India's technological capabilities would also strengthen the country's geopolitical status in the Global South and across the world.

The Minister said that the first thirty years of TDB were about building the bridge between the laboratory and the market, while the next thirty years should focus on building global technology champions from India. The accompanying address similarly emphasised the need to move from ideas to innovation, from innovation to industry and towards a truly developed India by 2047.

Dr. Jitendra Singh extended his good wishes to TDB and called for the institution to continue building on its role in technology development, public-private transition and technology self-reliance.

Bids were invited by NHAI for construction of the project in two packages and both packages received encouraging participation from the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Receives Overwhelming Response from Bidders for Construction of Coastal Corridor from Rameshwar to Paradeep in Odisha
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi

National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has received an overwhelming response from the bidders for the implementation of 160 km long Access Controlled Greenfield Coastal National Highway from Rameshwar to Paradeep in Odisha. Bids were invited by NHAI for construction of the project in two packages and both packages received encouraging participation from the bidders.

The 79.4 km long 4 lane access-controlled Rameshwar to Konark Package-I of the project received 10 bids, and 80.7 km long 2-lane with Paved Shoulder Konark to Paradeep Package-II received seven bids, reflecting robust competition and keen interest from the participants. The project will be awarded on Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM).

The new coastal Highway from Rameshwar to Paradeep project was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs in June 2026 with a combined total capital cost of Rs.8,300.79 crores. During construction, the project is expected to have a potential to generate 53.6 Lakhs direct man-days and 67 lakh indirect man-days of employment. 

With a design speed of 100 km/hour, the project will provide direct & fast connectivity to key tourist places like Sri Jagganath Temple, Puri Beach & Konark Sun Temple and help to reduce travel time between Rameshawar and Paradeep by about 2 hours and 30 minutes.

Rameshwar-Paradeep section of Coastal Highway will offer an alternate route for NH-16 & NH-316 and improve connectivity to Puri, Konark, Paradeep Port, upcoming Puri International Airport, facilitate smooth transportation to developing ports like Astarang and Subarnarekha as well as provide connectivity to Khurda, Puri, Kendrapada and Jagatsinghpur districts in Odisha.

The existing NH-16 is part of the Golden Quadrilateral and passes through major towns of Khordha, Bhubaneswar and Cuttack. Whereas NH-316 connects Bhubaneswar to Puri and further extends towards Satapada and Konark. The current sections along Puri–Satapada and Puri–Konark stretches has nearly 40% ribbon development along the corridor with high local commuter traffic, making the corridor unsuitable for high-speed long-distance vehicular movement.

The Rameshwar-Paradeep corridor will provide faster access-controlled connectivity, reduce fuel consumption, carbon emissions & vehicle operating costs, while lowering logistics costs and supporting economic growth across the region.

***

GDH/DS

item.title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews Progress of Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews Progress of Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana Average score of 100 Dhan-Dhaanya districts improves from 22.54 in April to 38.85 in July 2026 Focus on outcome-based monitoring, convergence of 36 schemes and ensuring benefits reach farmers Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today reviewed the progress of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) at Krishi Bhawan,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews Progress of Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
Average score of 100 Dhan-Dhaanya districts improves from 22.54 in April to 38.85 in July 2026
Focus on outcome-based monitoring, convergence of 36 schemes and ensuring benefits reach farmers
Posted On: 01 SEP 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today reviewed the progress of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. The review focused on accelerating implementation in the 100 identified districts, strengthening convergence among schemes, improving district-level performance and ensuring that interventions translate into measurable outcomes and tangible benefits for farmers.

 

During the review, the Minister was apprised of the progress of PM-DDKY through the scheme’s dashboard, including district-wise performance, District Action Plans, field monitoring by Central Nodal Officers (CNOs), financial progress, capacity building, convergence of schemes and mechanisms being developed to track beneficiary-level outcomes.

 

Data-driven monitoring of 100 districts

 

PM-DDKY aims to accelerate agricultural development in 100 districts identified on the basis of low agricultural productivity, low cropping intensity and low agricultural credit disbursement.

 

The scheme focuses on six key objectives: increasing agricultural productivity; promoting crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices; enhancing post-harvest storage capacity; improving irrigation infrastructure; enabling greater access to short- and long-term agricultural credit; and improving governance and service delivery.

 

The scheme is being implemented through the convergence of 36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private-sector participation.

 

A total of 121 indicators, comprising 74 output indicators and 47 outcome indicators, have been identified across the 36 schemes for monitoring progress against annual targets. District performance on output indicators is ranked every month through the PM-DDKY dashboard, while outcome indicators will facilitate assessment of progress against the baseline.

 

The average score of the 100 districts across the six objectives increased from 22.54 in April 2026 to 38.85 in July 2026, an improvement of 16.31 points.

 

Objective-wise performance also recorded improvement during the period. The average score for agricultural productivity increased from 2.53 in April to 6.70 in July; crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices from 5.60 to 8.65; post-harvest storage capacity from 2.61 to 3.82; irrigation infrastructure from 1.65 to 4.20; access to agricultural credit from 2.81 to 5.59; and governance and service delivery from 7.94 to 10.33.

 

All 100 districts have uploaded District Action Plans

 

The review noted that all 100 districts have uploaded their District Action Plans (DAPs) and feedback has been provided on the DAPs of all 100 districts.

 

All 100 districts have submitted data against output indicators up to July 2026, while all 100 districts have also submitted outcome-indicator data for the financial year 2025-26.

 

Committees have been constituted at the State, District and national levels for review and monitoring. Central Nodal Officers are also undertaking regular field-level monitoring of implementation.

 

Focus on outcomes and benefits reaching farmers

 

The review emphasised strengthening the monitoring framework to move beyond tracking activities and expenditure towards measuring outcomes and the actual benefits reaching farmers.

 

The Financial Progress Module of the PM-DDKY dashboard was implemented on 31 August 2026. A Beneficiary Progress Module is targeted for implementation by mid-September 2026 to enable systematic capture of beneficiary-level progress.

 

The strengthened dashboard will also facilitate consolidation of investments and interventions undertaken through Central schemes, State schemes and other sources in the Dhan-Dhaanya districts.

 

This will enable a comprehensive assessment of the resources deployed, activities undertaken, farmers benefited and outcomes achieved across the identified districts.

 

Capacity building of farmers and extension workers

 

Capacity development is an important component of PM-DDKY implementation. During January to July 2026, a total of 6,90,530 farmers and 88,961 extension workers were trained in various skills.

 

In addition, 2,20,683 farmers and extension workers were trained in natural farming during the period.

 

Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) are being utilised as technical partners for capacity development and field-level interventions, strengthening the agricultural extension system and facilitating dissemination of improved agricultural practices among farmers.

 

Strengthening convergence and partnerships

 

The review also focused on strengthening convergence among the 36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries and Departments, State schemes and private-sector interventions.

 

The Department of Public Enterprises has included adoption of PM-DDKY districts for CSR activities by Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) for 2026-27 and 2027-28, providing an additional avenue for supporting development interventions in the identified districts.

 

The monitoring mechanism is being strengthened to capture such convergence and investments, enabling assessment of the combined impact of interventions being implemented in the Dhan-Dhaanya districts.

 

PM-DDKY to complete one year in October

 

PM-DDKY was approved by the Union Cabinet on 16 July 2025 and officially launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 11 October 2025. The PM-DDKY dashboard was activated in the last week of October 2025, with monthly output-indicator rankings commencing from November 2025.

 

As the scheme approaches completion of its first year in October 2026, a programme is being planned to highlight the progress and performance of the 100 Dhan-Dhaanya districts. Progress will also be showcased during Rabi and regional conferences.

 

The review also considered convening a meeting of the National Executive Committee under the chairmanship of the Agriculture Minister and strengthening farmer participation through the proposed nomination of two progressive farmers in each District Dhan-Dhaanya Committee.

 

*****  

RC/MS

(Release ID: 2305501)
