item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
President of India Graces Combined Convocation Ceremony of NIFT in New Delhi
Students should maintain a Global Outlook while remaining firmly connected to their Roots and the Core Values of our Culture: President Droupadi Murmu
Combined Convocation Ceremony Celebrates Excellence and New Beginnings
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), under the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, marked a significant milestone in the lives of its graduating students with the Combined Convocation 2026 in New Delhi on 31 August 2026. The ceremony brought together graduates from 18 NIFT campuses across the country, turning the occasion into a collective celebration of academic accomplishment, creative endeavours and the journey from learning to professional life.

The ceremony was graced by the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, Visitor of NIFT, as the Chief Guest. Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh Secretary , Textiles Smt Neelam Shami Rao , DG,NIFT Smt Tanu Kashyap, distinguished dignitaries, members of the Board of Governors, senior officials, faculty members, PhD scholars and graduating students attended the event.

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the textile and apparel sector is not just a part of our cultural heritage, but it has also been the backbone of the livelihoods of millions of people. If the traditional artisans receive the support and guidance, it will encourage their next generations to remain engaged in this profession with pride and confidence. She was happy to note that various NIFT centres have implemented programmes like the 'Craft Cluster Initiative' to acquaint weavers and artisans in their respective regions with modern techniques in the textile and apparel sector and to connect them with markets. The President said that today, our country is expanding its role on the global stage with far greater confidence than ever before. Fashion Technology is also a field with immense potential to enhance India’s global footprint. She urged graduating students to seize this opportunity. She said that in this endeavour, students should maintain a global outlook while remaining firmly connected to their roots and the core values of our culture. By doing so, they will not only become successful professionals but also contribute to the preservation and enrichment of India’s cultural heritage.

Addressing the gathering Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh urged the students to dream big and work hard to become the integral driving force of Vikasit Bharat. Secretray Textiles Smt Neelam Shami Rao while congratulating the graduating students , asked them to pursue continuous learning and upgrading skills and thus to seize the vast opportunities.

The Convocation recognised the dedication and accomplishments of students who have completed their academic programmes at NIFT. Their time at the institute was shaped by exploration, collaboration and exposure to the changing needs of the fashion and creative industries.

During the Convocation, the Director General, NIFT administered the pledge to the graduating students and symbolically conferred degrees upon the graduating batch. A key highlight of the ceremony was the presentation of 10 Gold Medals to the Best Academic Performers, representing NIFT’s academic programmes across India. Selected on the basis of outstanding academic performance, taking into account their CGPA and semester-wise SGPA, the ten awardees were presented the Gold Medals by the Hon’ble President of India, recognising academic excellence across NIFT.

Following the central Convocation ceremony, campus-wise degree distribution ceremonies were held, providing graduates an opportunity to formally receive their degrees and celebrate the milestone alongside their respective academic communities.

Founded in 1986 under the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) is a statutory institute governed by the NIFT Act, 2006. The institute has played a pioneering role in shaping India’s fashion education landscape by creating an interdisciplinary learning environment where design, technology, craftsmanship, research, innovation and industry perspectives converge.

Across its 20 professionally managed campuses, NIFT continues to nurture diverse talent and encourage students to explore new ideas, challenge conventional approaches and develop solutions relevant to a rapidly changing creative economy. Its educational approach combines contemporary learning with an appreciation of India’s rich craft, cultural and design traditions.

For the graduating cohort, the 2026 Convocation represents a passage from preparation to possibility. The knowledge gained, projects undertaken, collaborations forged and challenges overcome during their time at NIFT will serve as building blocks for their careers and creative pursuits.

The graduates now join a growing community of NIFT alumni contributing across fashion, textiles, design, technology, entrepreneurship, communication and allied creative fields. With an understanding of both India’s cultural inheritance and contemporary global trends, they are poised to bring fresh perspectives to the industries and communities they serve.

The Combined Convocation 2026 with 3793 students graduating including Undergraduate, Post Graduate and PhD brought together achievement, aspiration and the promise of what lies ahead. As the graduates’ step into diverse professional and creative spaces, they carry with them the learning, values and experiences that have shaped their time at NIFT. Their journeys ahead will add new dimensions to India’s fashion, design and creative landscape, reflecting the talent and potential of a generation ready to create with purpose, lead with imagination and contribute to the making of a Viksit Bharat.

*****

Kumaraswamy Auto Industry Must Drive the Skilling Push as India Emerges as a Global Automotive Hub: H.D. Kumaraswamy ASDC’s Next Frontier: Building Skilled Automotive Talent for India and the World 43 Candidates Flagged Off for Romania as India Expands Global Opportunities for Skilled Youth Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
PM Modi’s Viksit Bharat Vision: India Must Build a Future-Ready Workforce for a Global Automotive Industry
Skilling India’s Youth for Jobs of Tomorrow and Opportunities Across the World: H.D. Kumaraswamy
Auto Industry Must Drive the Skilling Push as India Emerges as a Global Automotive Hub: H.D. Kumaraswamy
ASDC’s Next Frontier: Building Skilled Automotive Talent for India and the World
43 Candidates Flagged Off for Romania as India Expands Global Opportunities for Skilled Youth
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Heavy Industries H.D. Kumaraswamy on Monday underlined the need to make skilling, upskilling and employment generation for India’s younger generation a central priority as the country moves towards Viksit Bharat @2047, stressing that India’s skilled workforce must be prepared not only to meet domestic requirements but also the growing needs of industries across the world.

Addressing the Automotive Skills Development Council (ASDC) Annual Conclave 2026 in New Delhi, the Union Minister said India’s automotive sector is entering a new era of transformation, driven by electric mobility, automation, connected technologies, advanced manufacturing and Industry 4.0.

Highlighting the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Kumaraswamy said India is steadily moving beyond being merely a large automotive market and is emerging as a major global centre for automotive manufacturing, technology and mobility solutions.

“India’s ambition should not be limited to meeting our domestic manpower requirements. We must aspire to make India a global source of skilled automotive talent.”

The Minister emphasised that the rapid transformation of the automotive industry would require a workforce capable of adapting to new technologies and evolving workplace requirements. He said the focus must extend beyond simply training candidates to ensuring that young people acquire skills that translate into meaningful employment opportunities.

“Creating greater employment opportunities by skilling and upskilling our younger generation is essential not only for India, but for the entire world.”

He said the growing adoption of electric mobility, automation and advanced automotive technologies is creating new employment opportunities across vehicle manufacturing, battery production, charging infrastructure, servicing and after-sales support. This, he added, makes it imperative to develop technicians, engineers and professionals with specialised and industry-relevant capabilities.

Stronger Industry-Skill Linkage

Kumaraswamy stressed that the responsibility for building this workforce cannot rest with skilling institutions alone. Automobile manufacturers, component manufacturers, dealerships and other industry stakeholders will have a major role to play in defining the skills required for the future and ensuring that training reflects real-world requirements

“Skilling cannot succeed in isolation from the workplace. Industry participation is essential to ensure that training reflects real-world requirements and keeps pace with emerging technologies.”

He called for a stronger and more seamless relationship between education, skills and employment, with curricula, training methods and assessment systems continuously updated in consultation with industry.

The Minister said automobile manufacturers must actively participate in this process and help create a talent pipeline capable of meeting the requirements of an increasingly technology-driven industry.

“We need to build a stronger and more seamless relationship between education, skills and employment. Our skilling ecosystem must evolve alongside the growth and transformation of the automotive industry.”

ASDC’s Role in Building a Global Talent Pool

Kumaraswamy said institutions such as ASDC have an important role in ensuring that India’s workforce remains aligned with the changing requirements of the automotive sector.

He said ASDC must continue to work closely with industry to anticipate future requirements and equip young Indians with skills that are relevant both domestically and internationally.

The Minister said India should look beyond creating a workforce merely for its own requirements and position itself as a global supplier of skilled automotive professionals.

“Our responsibility is not merely to create certified candidates, but to create professionals who can contribute to India’s automotive growth and compete at global standards.”

He also underlined the importance of continuous upskilling and reskilling, particularly as new technologies rapidly change the nature of jobs in the automotive sector.

43 Candidates Flagged Off for Romania

During the programme, Kumaraswamy launched the ASDC Annual Report and flagged off 43 candidates placed in Romania, highlighting the growing international opportunities available to skilled Indian youth.

The Minister said such opportunities demonstrate how India’s investment in skills can create pathways for young Indians to participate in the global workforce.

The ASDC’s work is already expanding significantly. During FY 2025–26, the council impacted 5,08,173 learners, conducted 1,53,240 assessments and generated 2,88,756 apprenticeship contracts across approximately 3,700 establishments.

With the automotive industry undergoing a fundamental technological transformation, Kumaraswamy said the partnership between government, industry, academia and skilling institutions must become stronger.

“India has the ambition, the market and the manufacturing opportunity. Our collective responsibility is to ensure that we also have the skilled workforce capable of delivering on that ambition.”

He said the government would continue to support initiatives that strengthen manufacturing capabilities, promote technology adoption and develop the skills required for the industries of the future.

“A future-ready India requires a future-ready workforce. Through skilling, upskilling and strong industry participation, we can create opportunities for our youth in India and across the world.”

The Union Minister concluded by stressing that India’s demographic strength can become one of its greatest economic assets if the country succeeds in equipping its younger generation with the right skills and connecting those skills to employment opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attends Silver Jubilee celebrations of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology and inaugurates Confluence 3.0
Vice President calls for research-driven higher education and stronger industry-academia linkages
Keralam must focus on high-tech industries to create jobs and enable reverse migration: Vice President
“We just cannot produce graduates; we have to understand the demands of the market”: Vice President
“Say No to Drugs”: Vice President urges students to protect their dreams and aspirations
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the Silver Jubilee celebrations of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology (RSET) and inaugurated Confluence 3.0, an Industry-Academia Summit focused on “India, Impact of AI”, in Kochi.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Silver Jubilee celebrations of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology (RSET) and inaugurated Confluence 3.0, an Industry-Academia Summit focused on “India, Impact of AI”, in Kochi today.

Emphasising the changing demands… pic.twitter.com/84ww0GMd1d

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 31, 2026

Highlighting Keralam’s achievements in literacy, social development and human capital, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Rajagiri has contributed not only to producing technocrats but also leaders in public life. He congratulated the institution on completing 25 years and appreciated its commitment to combining values with technological excellence.

Recalling the contribution of the Carmelites of Mary Immaculate (CMI) and the legacy of Saint Kuriakose Elias Chavara, he highlighted their pioneering efforts in democratising education, promoting women’s education and adult literacy, and ensuring that poverty and hunger did not become barriers to learning.

Emphasising the changing demands of the technology-driven world, the Vice President said education cannot be limited to degrees. “We just cannot produce graduates; we have to understand the demands of the market,” he said, calling for greater emphasis on research, innovation and problem-solving.

Commending Confluence 3.0, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said stronger industry-academia partnerships are essential to make Bharat a global hub for technology and start-ups. He called for innovative teaching, interdisciplinary research, responsible use of AI and meaningful international collaborations while remaining rooted in Bharat’s values.

Referring to China’s transformation over the past few decades, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said its progress demonstrates the importance of sustained investment in higher education, research and innovation. He urged Keralam to strengthen research-oriented higher education and create an ecosystem that promotes innovation.

Appealing to the Chief Minister, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Keralam’s limited land availability and high land costs make large traditional industries challenging, and urged a greater focus on high-tech and knowledge-based industries. He said Keralam’s strong educational base and talent pool can attract high-technology enterprises, create local employment, reduce migration and enable reverse migration.

The Vice President made a strong appeal to young people to “Say No to Drugs.” Recalling his mother’s advice during his childhood, he said temporary pleasures can destroy great hopes and goals, and urged students to use their capabilities for the betterment of themselves, society and humanity.

The Vice President also laid the foundation stone for the Administrative Block of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology, marking another milestone in the institution’s journey of growth and academic excellence.

The programme was attended by the Governor of Keralam, Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar; Chief Minister of Keralam, Shri V. D. Satheesan; Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas and Tourism, Shri Suresh Gopi; Minister for Higher Education,Government of Keralam, Shri Roji M. John; and other dignitaries, including the management, faculty and students of RSET.

item.dc:creator: AYUSH

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
NHRIMH Kottayam Organises National Seminar on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Homoeopathy
Seminar explores AI-enabled clinical decision support, personalised care and ethical frameworks in Homoeopathic research
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

The National Homoeopathy Research Institute in Mental Health (NHRIMH), Kottayam, under the Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH), Ministry of Ayush organised a National Seminar on “Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Clinical Practice and Homoeopathy” today at the NHRIMH Auditorium, Kottayam. Organised under the theme “Where Intelligence Meets Compassion”, the seminar brought together experts, academicians, researchers, clinicians, practitioners and students to deliberate on the emerging applications of AI in healthcare and Homoeopathic research.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, addressed the programme virtually. In his address, the Minister highlighted the growing relevance of Artificial Intelligence in healthcare and the importance of informed discussions on its responsible application, particularly in the field of Homoeopathy.

The inaugural session was addressed by Dr. Subhash Kaushik, Director General, CCRH.  He emphasised the need for researchers and academicians to understand both the capabilities and ethical dimensions of AI to ensure its responsible application in healthcare and research.

The deliberations underscored that the adoption of AI in healthcare must be supported by human oversight, scientific validation, data credibility and appropriate ethical safeguards.

On the occasion, nine MoUs were signed with Homoeopathic Medical Colleges and Hospitals to strengthen academic collaboration in psychiatry and mental health. An MoU was also signed with Sevabharathi, Ettumanoor, for interdisciplinary research and institutional collaboration.

Dr. Debadatta Nayak, Assistant Director (Homoeopathy) and Officer-in-Charge, NHRIMH, said that representatives from around 12 Homoeopathic Medical Colleges across India, along with practitioners and faculty members from Kerala, participated in the seminar, providing a platform for academic exchange on AI in healthcare and Homoeopathy.

Dr. K. C. Muraleedharan, Deputy Director General, CCRH, Dr. Janardhanan Nair, Former President, Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB), National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH), and Prof. (Dr.) Eswara Das, Chairman, Regional Scientific Advisory Committee, NHRIMH, Kottayam, also addressed the gathering. The technical programme comprised four sessions focusing on AI in clinical decision support, applications of AI in Homoeopathy, and ethical aspects of AI in clinico-fundamental research.

The seminar reflects the commitment of CCRH and NHRIMH, Kottayam towards scientific innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration and responsible adoption of emerging technologies in Homoeopathic research and clinical practice. The initiative is expected to further strengthen academic and research networks and facilitate informed dialogue on the opportunities and challenges presented by AI in healthcare and Homoeopathy.

Ministry of Defence
IAF INTERNATIONAL SQUASH CHAMPIONSHIP 2026 COMMENCES AT CHANDIGARH
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 5:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Air Force International Squash Championship 2026 commenced at Base Repair Depot, Air Force Station Chandigarh marking the beginning of a prestigious international sporting event that brings together the finest squash talent from India and abroad.

The opening ceremony was graced by Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, Chief of the Air Staff as the Chief Guest. He welcomed all participants and highlighted the importance of international sports events in promoting camaraderie, mutual respect and friendship among the nations. The CAS also played a friendly match with Air Marshal M Baladitya (Retd) & Captain Dan Peskett of The United Kingdom.

The championship will culminate on 04 September 2026, and will feature six teams, including two international teams from The United Kingdom & Sri Lanka along with the veterans. The Championship features both team events and open singles category bringing together elite National and International squash players.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
SAMAVESH UTSAV to Celebrate Inclusion, Empowerment and Progress of DNT Communities
Event to Showcase Success Stories under the SEED Scheme and the Traditional Skills, Craftsmanship and Products of DNT Artisans
Around 700 Community Members, Leaders, Artisans and Beneficiaries Expected to Participate
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi

The Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC), under the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, is organizing “SAMAVESH UTSAV” at Bhim Hall, Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), in the National Capital tomorrow.

The event will be graced by Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment and Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment. Senior representatives of the DWBDNC, including Members Shri Bharatbhai Babubhai Patni and Shri Pravin Shivajirao Ghuge, will also grace the occasion.

Around 700 members of DNT communities, including community leaders, artisans and beneficiaries, are expected to participate in the event.

 

The event is part of initiatives to ensure inclusion, empowerment and progress of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic (DNT) communities.  

The stalls of DNT artisans and the Bharat-TULIP Heritage Store, will be set up during the event. The success stories under the Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs (SEED), along with the traditional skills, craftsmanship and products of artisans belonging to these communities, will remain other features of the event. The other initiatives undertaken by the Central Government for the welfare of DNT communities, will also be highlighted.

To implement welfare and development programmes the Central Government constituted The Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic, and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC) through a notification dated 21st February 2019.

The Government subsequently launched the Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNTs (SEED) to support the holistic welfare of DNT communities in the areas of education, health, livelihood and housing. The scheme is being implemented in eight States—Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh where DNT certificates are being issued by the respective State Governments.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Monthly Review of Accounts of Union Government of India upto the month of July 2026 (FY 2026-27)
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Monthly Accounts of the Union Government of India upto the month of July, 2026 has been consolidated and reports published. The highlights are given below: -

The Government of India has received ₹13,06,709 crore (35.8% of corresponding BE 2026-27 of Total Receipts) upto July, 2026 comprising ₹8,44,560 crore Tax Revenue (Net to Centre), ₹4,23,013 crore of Non-Tax Revenue and ₹39,136 crore of Non-Debt Capital Receipts. ₹3,72,354 crore has been transferred to State Governments as Devolution of Share of Taxes by Government of India during this period which is ₹56,190 crore lower than the previous year.

Total Expenditure incurred by Government of India is ₹17,61,853 crore (32.9% of corresponding BE 2026-27), out of which ₹13,11,218 crore is on Revenue Account and ₹4,50,635 crore is on Capital Account. Out of the Total Revenue Expenditure, ₹4,26,566 crore is on account of Interest Payments and ₹1,53,513 crore is on account of Major Subsidies.

item.title: Century-old limit on turning heat into electricity surpassed, enabling ultrasensitive temperature sensing
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology Century-old limit on turning heat into electricity surpassed, enabling ultrasensitive temperature sensing Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi Scientists have stumbled on to a crystalline semiconductor that converts a temperature difference into an electrical voltage nearly a thousand times larger than textbook physics allows. The thermoelectric voltage generated is so large that it rivals values normally seen only in liquid electrolytes and ionic gels, not in solid, particularly single-crystalline materials. The discovery…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Century-old limit on turning heat into electricity surpassed, enabling ultrasensitive temperature sensing
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi

Scientists have stumbled on to a crystalline semiconductor that converts a temperature difference into an electrical voltage nearly a thousand times larger than textbook physics allows.

The thermoelectric voltage generated is so large that it rivals values normally seen only in liquid electrolytes and ionic gels, not in solid, particularly single-crystalline materials.

The discovery overturns a decades-old assumption about the ceiling on this effect in solids and opens a path to a new generation of ultrasensitive temperature sensors, heat detectors, and quantum sensing devices.

When one end of a junction between two dissimilar materials is heated while the other is kept cold, mobile charge carriers drift from the hot side to the cold side, building up a voltage across the junctions. This phenomenon, known as the Seebeck effect, was discovered two centuries ago and underlies technologies ranging from temperature sensors to thermoelectric generators that convert waste heat into electricity.

For decades, the size of this voltage, quantified as the Seebeck coefficient, places an upper bound of only a few millivolts per Kelvin on this effect in a crystalline solid. Most metals generate just tens of microvolts per Kelvin, and even good semiconductors rarely exceed a few hundred microvolts per Kelvin. Only liquid systems, such as ionic gels and electrolytes, in which charged ions rather than electrons carry the heat, have been known to cross into the millivolts-per-Kelvin range.

A group of researchers from the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), along with University of Sydney, Australia, and Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore, has now shown that this textbook limit can be shattered in a solid, epitaxial crystal.

The team led by Prof. Bivas Saha along with Renuka Karanje and Dheemahi Rao and colleagues Diksha Dadhich and Sourav Rudra from JNCASR, Ashalatha Indiradevi Kamalasanan Pillai and Dr. Magnus Garbrecht from University of Sydney and Prof. Subroto Mukerjee from IISc, grew thin films of scandium nitride (ScN), a refractory transition-metal nitride, on magnesium oxide substrates using ultrahigh-vacuum magnetron sputtering.

They deliberately doped them with magnesium to compensate the material's naturally occurring free electrons from oxygen dopants. This produced what is known as a heavily doped, highly compensated (HDHC) semiconductor, a material in which positively and negatively charged dopant atoms are scattered randomly throughout the crystal in nearly equal numbers.

X-ray diffraction and atomic-resolution electron microscopy confirmed that the films remained single-crystalline and epitaxial, with dopant atoms distributed uniformly and no secondary phases or precipitates.

In these HDHC ScN films, the team measured a Seebeck coefficient several hundred to over a thousand times larger than the value typically seen in inorganic semiconductors, and nearly a hundred times beyond the earlier known ceiling (exceeding –124.6 millivolts per Kelvin near room temperature, in a roughly 200-nanometre-thick film). This places it firmly above the range previously associated even with liquid electrolytes and ionic conductors such as hydrogels and ionic gelatin.

The researchers describe the result as a solid-state analog of electrolyte-like thermopower inside a fully crystalline semiconductor.

The effect grew even stronger as the HDHC ScN films were made thinner.

“We were not looking for a record-breaking number when we started this work; we were trying to understand how disorder and charge compensation reshape electronic transport in scandium nitride,” said Prof. Bivas Saha, who led the study. “What we found instead is that a fully crystalline, epitaxial, single-phase semiconductor can behave thermoelectrically like a liquid electrolyte. That was genuinely surprising, and it tells us that engineered disorder is a largely untapped route to extreme thermoelectric and sensing performance in solids.”

Fig 1: Schematic of the electronic band diagram of heavily doped, highly compensated ScN exhibiting thermopower exceeding the Boltzmann limit.

 

The team has built a preliminary prototype photon sensor using an HDHC ScN film with two chromium contacts. Illuminating one contact with a laser created a tiny, localized temperature difference across the device, and the resulting voltage translated to a Seebeck response of –102.4 millivolts per Kelvin, comfortably large enough for classical light detection and, the team suggests, potentially for single-photon-level detection near room temperature with further optimization. The voltage response was fast, repeatable over multiple illumination cycles, and left the material unchanged. An Indian patent application has been filed by the team on thermoelectric thin-film materials and sensors for temperature and photon detection based on this work.

Fig 2: (Left-to-right) JNCASR team, Prof. Bivas Saha, Sourav Rudra, Diksha Dadhich, Renuka Karanje and Dheemahi Rao

 

The findings published in the prestigious journal Science point to applications in ultrasensitive temperature sensing, low-noise thermal imaging, high-resolution heat-flux detection, bolometric devices, and Internet-of-Things sensors, as well as cryogenic thermoelectric single-photon detectors relevant to emerging quantum technologies. The team also notes that the steep, well-defined temperature dependence of the effect could enable temperature-controlled Seebeck switches for future device applications.

Publication Link: DOI: 10.1126/science.aef9458

Contact Information: Prof. Bivas Saha (bsaha@jncasr.ac.in)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INS NIPUN COMMISSIONED INTO THE INDIAN NAVY
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy commissioned INS Nipun, the second Diving Support Vessel (DSV) of the Nistar Class, at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai, on 31 Aug 2026, marking a significant enhancement of the Navy’s deep-sea diving, underwater intervention and submarine rescue capabilities.

The commissioning ceremony was presided over by Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, in the presence of Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command. Senior naval officers, representatives from Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), Visakhapatnam, veterans, distinguished guests and families of the commissioning crew were also in attendance.

Indigenously designed and constructed by Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam, INS Nipun is a significant addition to the Indian Navy’s specialist underwater capability. Her induction demonstrates India’s growing capability to design and build technologically complex specialist naval platforms and is another significant step towards Aatmanirbharta in defence shipbuilding. It also reflects the contribution of Indian shipyards, domestic industry and associated agencies towards strengthening the Navy’s indigenous capability.

INS Nipun is a purpose-built platform designed primarily for deep-sea diving and underwater operations. The ship is capable of supporting saturation, air and heliox diving and is equipped with remotely operated underwater systems for inspection and intervention. Her specialised diving complex, dynamic positioning capability and associated life-support and medical facilities enable sustained and complex operations at sea.

INS Nipun is also capable of supporting submarine rescue operations, significantly strengthening the Indian Navy’s ability to respond to underwater contingencies. Along with her sister ship INS Nistar, the ship substantially enhances the Navy’s specialist capability in diving, underwater intervention, salvage and submarine rescue.

The ship’s crest and motto embody the spirit of her specialised role and the men who venture into the depths. The motto, ‘Far Beneath, Few Beyond’, reflects the resolve, skill and endurance required to operate in one of the most challenging domains of the maritime environment.

In his address, CNS stated that the induction of INS Nipun reflects the seamless synergy between the Indian Navy, Hindustan Shipyard Limited and the domestic industrial network. He further stated that proving the role-worthiness of all diving systems during sea trials in a single sortie stands as a testament to the nation’s technical confidence and engineering prowess.

CNS emphasised that combat readiness remains the Indian Navy’s highest priority amidst an increasingly contested maritime environment and growing threats to global maritime highways. He noted that, based on the West Coast under the Western Naval Command, INS Nipun will be a powerful addition to the specialised underwater capabilities required to sustain multi-domain operations.

The CNS highlighted that the niche capabilities of INS Nipun, available with only a handful of global navies, enable a swift response to distressed submarines of the Indian Navy as well as partner nations. This capability positions India as the ‘Preferred Submarine Rescue Partner’ in the region, while also providing specialised support for underwater salvage and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) missions.

Addressing the commissioning crew, CNS stated that they inherit not just a sophisticated platform, but also the onerous responsibility to shape the ship’s soul and instil spirit into her steel. Exhorting the crew to live up to the ship’s motto of ‘Nischay, Nirbhay, Nipun’ (Resolve, Fearlessness and Professional Mastery), he urged them to remain anchored in the core naval values of Duty, Honour and Courage.

With the hoisting of the Commissioning Pennant, INS Nipun has formally entered operational service with the Indian Navy, ready to support those who operate beneath the waves and contribute to safeguarding India’s maritime interests.

________________________________________________________________

VM/AS                                                                                                        158/26

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
National Conference on Quantum Biotechnology charts India's path in quantum-enabled life sciences
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

India’s quantum science and life sciences communities came together at the National Conference on Quantum Biotechnology with representation from researchers, clinicians, industry leaders, startups, and students, to advance the translation of quantum science into diagnostics, biomedical imaging, drug discovery, and precision medicine, in alignment with India’s National Quantum Mission (NQM).

Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST), highlighted the strategic importance of quantum biotechnology while delivering the keynote address at the inaugural session of the one-day national conference hosted by Qmet Tech recently at the PC Saxena Auditorium on the IIT Bombay campus, Mumbai, Maharashtra. QMet Tech Foundation (Qmet) is the thematic hub (T-hub) for Quantum Sensing & Metrology set up under NQM at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay campus, with support from DST.

Quantum biotechnology sits at the intersection of quantum sensing, imaging, and computing with the life sciences - an emerging frontier where quantum-grade measurement is beginning to unlock biological questions that conventional instrumentation cannot reach. The conference was designed as an interdisciplinary platform to define national research directions in this space and to strengthen the pathway from laboratory demonstration to deployable healthcare technology.

“Unless we work on all sides of the technology in an integrated and strategic manner, we cannot take India ahead in the technology domain,” Prof. Shireesh Kedare, Director, IIT Bombay said, highlighting the institute’s role in convening interdisciplinary national platforms.

"Quantum biotechnology is where our sensing capabilities meet real clinical needs. At Qmet Tech, we are building quantum sensors of remarkable precision. The task now is to point them at the questions biology has been unable to answer. Bringing physicists, biologists, and industry into one room is how that translation begins," underlined Prof. Kasturi Saha, Project Director, Qmet Tech Foundation, on Qmet Tech’s quantum sensing capabilities and their application to biosensing.

"What struck me today is how much industry interest quantum biotechnology is attracting. Qmet Tech's role is to convert it into deployable technology, supporting startups, developing talent, and creating the manufacturing and testing capability India will need as these tools move towards the clinic, " said Hardik Joshi, CEO Qmet Tech Foundation.

The programme was structured around three sessions. These were on quantum for biology and the academic landscape, translating quantum biosensors--from lab to industry and innovating for applications in biosensing. A panel discussion was held on ‘Quantum Biotechnology in India: Opportunities, Challenges, and the Path Forward’.

Dr. JBV Reddy, Head, Quantum Technology Cell, DST, Dr. Rajneesh Gaur, Scientist ‘F’, Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Prof. Himadri Dhar, IIT Bombay, as well as Prof. Swaroop Ganguly, IIT Bombay, Mr. Hardik Joshi, CEO, Qmet Tech Foundation participated in the deliberations.

By bringing quantum sensing, imaging, computing, and biotechnology into a single forum, the National Conference on Quantum Biotechnology reinforced the National Quantum Mission’s objective of building a collaborative, application-driven quantum ecosystem and positioning quantum-enabled life sciences as a priority frontier for India’s research and healthcare innovation agenda.

 

Fig 1: Prof. Umesh Waghmare, Secretary, DST, addressing the inaugural session of the national conference       

Fig 2: A group photograph of conference participants.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Reviews Progress of Rural Health Training Centre, Najafgarh
Directs time-bound completion of ongoing works and further strengthening of clinical, academic and training infrastructure
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda today chaired a review meeting to assess the progress of the Rural Health Training Centre (RHTC), Najafgarh, and reviewed the implementation of initiatives aimed at strengthening patient care, infrastructure, manpower, academic activities and digital health systems at the Centre.

Reviewing the progress since the meeting held on April 13, 2026, Shri Nadda directed all concerned agencies and institutions to ensure timely completion of ongoing works and coordinated implementation of planned interventions. He emphasised close monitoring of deliverables, timely availability of manpower and equipment, and continued focus on quality patient care and medical training.

The Centre’s OPD and Emergency services are fully operational, along with the Anti-Rabies Vaccination Centre, Anti-Snake Venom Centre and other supporting facilities viz., Jan Aushadhi Kendra, CSSD, laboratory and ambulance services. The Minor Operation Theatre is functional.

RHTC Najafgarh has also been onboarded onto MedLeapR, for medico-legal cases, and onto PM-JAY under Ayushman Bharat, facilitating access to services for eligible beneficiaries.  RHTC is progressing towards NQAS certification of its UPHCs and development of Model PHCs.

On an average monthly basis, RHTC recorded around 47,000 OPD consultations and 9,000 emergency attendances, besides 221 minor procedures done in August, 2026. TB symptom screening has been integrated into routine OPD and PHC interactions under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan.

RHTC is collaborating with other Central Government institutions including Safdarjung Hospital, ABVIMS, Dr. RML Hospital and NIMR for strengthening clinical manpower, training, digital systems, procurement and research. The Centre has also joined the One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) initiative.

During the review, Shri Nadda noted that RHTC Najafgarh has made significant progress in strengthening its clinical manpower and services.  He further reiterated the importance of coordinated and time-bound action to further develop RHTC Najafgarh as a comprehensive centre for patient care, medical education, nursing and allied health training, and community-oriented healthcare.

The meeting was attended by Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava; Director General of Health Services, Government of India, Dr. Loveneesh G Krishna; Joint Secretaries Shri Saurabh Jain, Dr. Manashvi Kumar & G.S. Chitra along with Director, VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital Dr. Kavita Rani Sharma; Director, RHTC Najafgarh Dr. B K Kundu; and other senior officers of the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.

*****

SR

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Department of Fertilizers to Observe ‘Swachhata Pakhwada-2026’ from September 1 to 15, 2026
Special Thrust on Digital Record Maintenance, e-Office Optimization and Paperless Cleanliness Alongside Physical Upkeep
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fertilizers, under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, is observing ‘Swachhata Pakhwada-2026’ from 1st to 15th September, 2026. The primary objective of this nationwide campaign is to foster cleanliness at both physical and digital workplaces, promote environmental conservation, and bring qualitative improvements to work culture. This year, alongside physical cleanliness, special priority is being accorded to ‘Digital Cleanliness and Record Management’ to enhance administrative efficiency, transparency, and further strengthen the e-filing system.

Campaign Focused on Digital Record Management and Data Hygiene:

In view of modern administrative requirements, the Department of Fertilizers has formulated a dedicated strategy for digital cleanliness. Under this initiative, the e-Office and digital filing systems will be streamlined. This includes reviewing pending e-files in the e-Office system, digitally closing/archiving disposed cases, and systematizing databases. Additionally, departmental personnel are being encouraged to purge redundant, spam, and obsolete files/attachments from their official email inboxes to optimize server space.

Union Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda to Inaugurate the Pakhwada:

The Swachhata Pakhwada will commence with an inspiring cleanliness message from Union Minister of Health & Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda. As part of the inaugural proceedings, the Swachhata Pledge will be administered to all officers and staff of the Department. Concurrently, public awareness will be generated regarding the elimination of single-use plastics and promoting the use of cloth bags and reusable bottles.

 Key Schedule of Activities & Programmes:

  • September 2 (Physical Record Management): Inspection of physical record rooms; identification and weeding out of old/obsolete files as per Record Retention Rules.
  • September 3 (Green Workplace Initiative): Distribution of awareness-themed cotton T-shirts and a plantation drive led by senior officers.
  • September 7 (Scrap Disposal): Identification and systematic disposal of condemned equipment, obsolete furniture, and e-waste through prescribed procedures.
  • September 8 (Public Grievance Redressal): Expedited review and disposal of pending references received via CPGRAMS, PMO, Members of Parliament, and State Governments.
  • September 9 (Digital Cleanliness Day): A dedicated, department-wide digital sanitization drive focusing on the clean-up and systematic organization of e-files, cloud drives, and official mailboxes.
  • September 10 (Community Shramdaan): Collective voluntary clean-up drives (Shramdaan) across office premises and surrounding zones by all officials.
  • September 11 (Hygiene & Infrastructure Audit): Signature campaign for sustainability and rigorous safety audits of drinking water facilities and sanitation amenities.
  • September 14 (Creative Engagement): Essay writing and ideation contests for staff on institutionalizing cleanliness and digital efficiency.

The Department of Fertilizers urges all officers, staff members and affiliated organizations to actively participate in Swachhata Pakhwada-2026, embracing both physical and digital cleanliness as a sustainable daily practice to build a smarter, greener, and more responsive administrative ecosystem.

***

Neeraj Kumar Bhatt/Amit/Shatrughna Prasad

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR-IIOR to host National Consultation and Industry Interface Meet to Accelerate Commercialization of Oilseed Technologies in Hyderabad
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:33PM by PIB Delhi

The ICAR–Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research (ICAR-IIOR), Hyderabad will organise a National Consultation and Industry Interface Meet on “Innovations in Varieties/Hybrids, Biologicals and Biopolymer-Enabled Multilayer Seed Coating Technologies for Sustainable Agriculture: Industry Partnerships for Technology Commercialization and Scaling” on 10th September 2026 at ICAR-IIOR, Hyderabad.

India is one of the world’s major vegetable oil economies, and increasing demand for edible oils, coupled with need to accelerate domestic oilseed production, necessitates accelerated technology development, commercialization and adoption to strengthen self-reliance. In this context, ICAR-IIOR has developed promising technologies, including improved oilseed varieties and hybrids, biopolymer-enabled seed enhancement technologies, and microbial biopesticide formulations.

The meet will bring together representatives from the seed industry, biopesticide and bio-input companies, technology licensees, agri-business firms, start-ups and entrepreneurs, while ICAR-IIOR will showcase its promising technologies and explore opportunities for technology transfer, licensing, public–private partnerships and large-scale deployment.

The initiative is expected to strengthen research–industry linkages and stakeholder collaboration, facilitating the validation, commercialization and adoption of innovative technologies for the benefit of farmers and the sustainable growth of India’s oilseed sector.

*****

RC/MS

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Bilateral meeting between Prime Minister and the President of the Kyrgyz Republic
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:33PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met H.E. Mr. Sadyr Zhaparov, President of the Kyrgyz Republic, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation organization (SCO) Summit in Bishkek on 31 August 2026.

Prime Minister warmly congratulated President Zhaparov on the occasion of the Independence Day of the Kyrgyz Republic, noting that it gave a special meaning to the opening of the SCO Summit the same day. He also congratulated President Zhaparov for hosting the 26th SCO Summit. The two leaders reviewed the progress made in bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the Strategic Partnership between India and the Kyrgyz Republic. They agreed to further enhance economic and commercial cooperation, taking into account the complementarities between the two economies. They also discussed growing people-to-people ties, including through student exchanges and cultural collaborations.

Prime Minister highlighted India’s strong participation in the meetings of the SCO held under the Chairmanship of the Kyrgyz Republic. He further added that this reflected the mutual respect, trust and support that characterizes the close and longstanding relations between the two countries. Prime Minister thanked President Sadyr Zhaparov for his warmth and hospitality and for successfully conducting the SCO Summit.

 

***

MJPS/SS/VJ

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) releases the 48th Report on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) for States/UTs for July, 2026
A total of 1,01,047 PG cases received for the States/UTs and 83,324 PG cases redressed in July, 2026
Under the Sevottam Scheme, in the last five Financial Years, 1,217 training courses completed, in which about 40,077 officers have been trained
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) released the Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) 48th monthly report for States/UTs for July, 2026. The said report provides a detailed analysis of types and categories of public grievances and the nature of disposal by the States/UTs.

In July, 2026, 1,01,047 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 83,324 PG cases were redressed. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in July, 2026 with 24,694 PG cases, followed by Rajasthan with 6,774 PG cases. As of 31st July, 2026, the total pendency of PG cases on the CPGRAMS portal stands at 2,33,714 across all States and UTs. Moreover, 22 States/UTs have more than 1,000 pending PG cases each.

The report provides the data for new users registered on CPGRAMS through CPGRAMS Portal during July, 2026. A total of 1,07,186 new users have registered on CPGRAMS in July, 2026, through various channels, out of which, 17,819 registrations are from Uttar Pradesh.

The said report also provides the state-wise analysis on the grievances registered through Common Service Centres in July, 2026. CPGRAMS has been integrated with the Common Service Centre (CSC) portal and is available at more than 5 lakh CSCs, associating with 2.5 lakh Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). A total of 9,475 grievances have been registered through the Common Service Centres in the month of July, 2026.

The report also provides the total number of training programmes conducted and officers trained over the last five financial years under the Sevottam Scheme. Between FY 2022–23 and FY 2026–27, a total of 1,217 training courses were conducted, training ~40,077 officers.

Key Highlights for the month of July, 2026, are as follows:

General Highlights

  • To facilitate senior-level review of PG cases in States/UTs, a dedicated Review Module has been operationalised, effective from 6th July 2025.
  • Under the Sevottam Scheme, in the last five Financial Years (FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27), 1,217 training courses have been completed, in which ~40,077 officers have been trained.
  • The National Conference on e-Governance (NCeG) was held in Jaipur on 1st and 2nd July. As part of the exhibition, a dedicated stall on the CPGRAMS Portal was set up.

Status of Public Grievances on CPGRAMS

  • In July, 2026, 1,01,047 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 83,324 PG cases were redressed.
  • Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in July, 2026 with 24,694 PG cases, followed by Rajasthan with 6,774 PG cases.

Status of Pendency of Public Grievances on CPGRAMS

  • 22 States/UTs have more than 1000 pending grievances as on 31st July, 2026.
  • For States/UTs, as on 31st July, 2026, there exists a pendency of 2,33,714 PG cases

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
NPCI International and Uzbekistan’s NIPC Partner to Enable UPI Payments Across Uzbekistan via UZQR
Indian tourists, business travellers and students can make instant merchant payments by scanning Uzbekistan’s national interoperable QR code, UZQR
Partnership between NIPL and Uzbekistan’s National payment system marks a significant step in expanding UPI’s international footprint
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi

NPCI International Payments Ltd. (NIPL), the international arm of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), has entered into a commercial agreement with the National Interbank Processing Centre JSC (NIPC), operator of Uzbekistan’s national payment system, HUMO, on 30th August 2026. The partnership enables Indian travellers to scan Uzbekistan’s national interoperable QR code UZQR using their familiar UPI-enabled applications to make instant merchant payments across the country.

The announcement was made during the bilateral visit of the Prime Minister of India to Uzbekistan. The execution of the agreement follows formal approvals from financial regulators, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Central Bank of Uzbekistan (CBU), which designated HUMO as NIPL’s authorised partner for cross-border merchant acceptance.

Key Highlights of the Agreement

  1. Universal Merchant Acceptance: By integrating with CBU’s mandated Unified National QR infrastructure (UZQR), UPI users gain near-universal acceptance across retail, hospitality, and service merchants in Uzbekistan.
  2. Seamless Travel Experience: Indian tourists, business travellers, and students can make direct person-to-merchant (P2M) payments from their Indian bank accounts, eliminating foreign exchange markup friction and reducing reliance on international cards or cash.
  3. Strengthened Bilateral Ties: The initiative advances digital public infrastructure cooperation and aligns with both nations' broader strategic and economic goals.

UPI is Accepted in Ten Countries

Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, and Greece, enabling Indian travellers to make seamless payments abroad through UPI.

****

SR/AD

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw addressed media on Semicon 2.0
Notifications for all 6 Pillars of Semicon 2.0 issued
India achieved target of developing 85,000 semiconductor engineers in four years against 10-year target: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Close to 10% of the global semiconductor industry’s market will be in India in the coming years: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Students from Tier-II and Tier-III cities have designed more than 250 semiconductor chips: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Posted On: 31 AUG 2026 4:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways and Information & Broadcasting, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, today addressed the media and outlined the Government’s vision for taking India’s semiconductor ecosystem to the next level. On the occasion, notifications for all six pillars of the Semicon 2.0 Scheme were issued, marking a significant step towards strengthening India’s semiconductor design and manufacturing capabilities.

The scheme builds on the momentum generated by the first Semicon India Programme and provides fiscal and infrastructure support across the semiconductor value chain from chip design, fabrication and packaging to equipment, materials, research and development, and talent development.

The scheme aims to strengthen India’s economic growth and national security by improving semiconductor supply-chain resilience and establishing technological leadership in critical sectors. It will operate through six pillars covering 10 categories.

The six pillars under Semicon 2.0 are:

• Pillar 1 -  Design

• Pillar 2 - Machines and Materials

• Pillar 3 - Setting up more Fabs

• Pillar 4 - Further strengthening the ATMP/OSAT industry

• Pillar 5 - Research and Development

• Pillar 6 - Talent Development

Pillar 1 - Design: Categories: Design of Semiconductor IPs, Chips, System-on-Chips (SoCs), and Modules for National Importance and Strategic Priorities; Design of Semiconductor IPs, Chips and SoCs for the Commercial Sector; and Deployment-Linked Incentive (DLI) for Semiconductor IPs/Chips/SoCs for deployment.

Pillar 2  - Machines and Materials: Category: Semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.

Pillar 3 - Setting up more Fabs: Categories: Silicon Semiconductor Wafer Fabs; Compound Semiconductors/Photonics/Sensors (including MEMS) Fab/Discrete Semiconductors Fab; and Display Fabs.

Pillar 4 - Further strengthening the ATMP/OSAT industry: Category: Semiconductor Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) / Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) Facility.

Pillar 5  -  Research and Development: Category: R&D for advanced semiconductor technologies.

Pillar 6  -  Talent Development: Category: Talent Development.

During the event Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said “India achieved its target of developing 85,000 semiconductor engineers over a period of 10 years in just four years, and has now set a new target of developing one lakh more engineers. In the coming years, close to 10% of the global semiconductor industry’s market is expected to be in India. Students from Tier-II and Tier-III cities have already designed more than 250 chips. In one case, commercial production commenced within just 13 months of the groundbreaking, while approvals were granted within 200 days, 150 days and even 90 days in multiple cases. The semiconductor ecosystem being developed in India is also expected to create 50,000–60,000 direct jobs.”

Projects supported under Semicon 2.0 will generally have a duration of up to six years, while the scheme will initially remain open for applications for three years.

The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) will be the nodal agency for Semicon 2.0. It will invite applications, undertake technical and financial appraisal, recommend applicants and oversee implementation. ISM may implement the design and deployment categories with the assistance of C-DAC. The mission may also announce semiconductor deep-tech awards from 2026 to promote niche innovation.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology will make budgetary provisions for fiscal support, with disbursements undertaken by the nodal agency in accordance with approved conditions. A mid-term assessment will be conducted after three years of implementation, or as required, to evaluate the scheme’s impact and consider modifications or continuation.

For the notification, you can visit  Semicon 2.0

You can watch the Press Conference here

Vinod Kumar/Vanshita Jaiswal/Aparajita Priyadarshini

The meeting was also attended by Home Secretary-cum-Secretary, Local Government, UT Chandigarh, Sh. Mandip Singh Brar,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal reviews Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban progress in Chandigarh; Directs Fast-track Project Implementation & Strengthening of Swachhata
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, chaired a review meeting on the progress of the Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U) in Chandigarh, held at the UT Guest House.

The meeting was also attended by Home Secretary-cum-Secretary, Local Government, UT Chandigarh, Sh. Mandip Singh Brar, IAS; Commissioner, Municipal Corporation Chandigarh, Sh. Amit Kumar, IAS; Deputy Commissioner, Chandigarh, Sh. Nishant Yadav, IAS; Special Commissioner, MCC, Sh. Harpreet Singh Sudan, IAS, besides senior officers of the Chandigarh Administration and Municipal Corporation, along with senior government officials from MoHUA, Director, SBM-U, Ms. Surabhi Malik and Advisor, CPHEEO, Ankit Jain, State government officials from Urban development department.

During the review, the Hon’ble Minister underscored the need to fast‑track Aspirational Toilet construction while ensuring that all existing facilities (CT/PTs) are regularly monitored, maintained, and kept fully functional and accessible to the public at all times.

He also reviewed preparations for the upcoming 15-day Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, directing that the Swachhata Pakhwada must actively engage citizens in every initiative during the 15‑day campaign. He emphasized that citizens are the true custodians of Swachhata, and their feedback must not only be heard but acted upon with utmost seriousness.The Hon'ble Minister highlighted that all processing facilities, waste collection vehicles, and government offices must be cleaned — just as homes are readied before Diwali — so that every element associated with swachhata reflects renewed commitment.

He further advocated cross‑learning among Urban Local Bodies, pointing to best practices from Integrated Command and Control Centres where AI and digital tools are used to track vehicles, capture real‑time data and derive smart solutions.

The Union Minister directed that a structured city‑to‑city learning mechanism be institutionalized, enabling knowledge sharing of processes, facilities, and innovations. The cities showcasing these best practices should be made accessible to the others for streamlining processes in various cities.

Satisfied with Chandigarh’s progress under SBM‑U 2.0, the Hon’ble Minister reiterated that beyond achieving swachhata, the greater responsibility lies in sustaining and continuously improving it.

***

SK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Biodiversity Authority disburses Rs. 5.68 Crore in Access and Benefit-Sharing Funds for Biodiversity Conservation
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 5.68 crore under the Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism arising from the utilisation of biological resources. The funds have been channelled to State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) and a national research institution, primarily in relation to Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), Cucumber (Cucumis sativus) and Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), besides specified microbial and agricultural biological resources.

The largest ABS component relates to Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), covering 139 varieties and 28 hybrids, for which the NBA has released Rs. 3.51 crore to 32 State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils. The ABS amount was received from M/s. Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd. in connection with its access to Okra.

The other major ABS components relate to Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), covering 662 varieties and 15 hybrids and Cucumber (Cucumis sativus), covering 1009 varieties and 14 hybrids. These biological resources were accessed through markets/traders by M/s. Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd., M/s. East West Seeds India Pvt. Ltd. and M/s. Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd.

In these cases, the biological resources were accessed from markets and traders, making it not feasible to trace them to specific individual farmers, communities or a single identifiable geographic source. Accordingly, the modality recommended by the Expert Committee and approved by the Authority provides for distribution of the beneficiary share among the States and Union Territories where the concerned biological resource is cultivated.

In addition, the NBA has disbursed benefit-sharing funds to CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory (NCL) – National Culture of Industrial Microorganisms, Pune, from an ABS amount received from M/s. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd., Mumbai.

The funds disbursed to the SBBs and UTBCs are to be utilised as per Section 32 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, for activities supporting the objectives of the Act. These include documentation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers; conservation and sustainable use of biological resources; restoration of degraded ecosystems; protection of wild relatives of cultivated plants; strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites; development and maintenance of biodiversity databases; capacity building; research; and community-oriented livelihood enhancement activities.

The funds disbursed to the research institution are to support activities including maintenance of repositories of biological resources, research and bio-survey activities, capacity building in taxonomy and conservation, and in-situ and ex-situ conservation.

With this disbursement, the total ABS amount disbursed by the NBA so far has crossed Rs. 191 crore. The disbursements reaffirm the NBA's commitment to ensuring that benefits arising from the utilisation of India's biological resources are directed towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, strengthening of institutional capacities and activities benefiting communities and other stakeholders associated with the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister lays wreath at Shastri Memorial and visits Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister today paid floral tributes at the Shastri Memorial in Tashkent. This year marks the 60th anniversary of the passing away of the former Prime Minister in Tashkent in 1965. The memorial is situated on a street named after Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. The life and legacy of the former Prime Minister is fondly remembered in Tashkent. In addition to the memorial and the street, there is a local school and the Indian Cultural Centre in Tashkent named after him.

After offering respects at the Shastri Memorial, Prime Minister visited the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies. At the university, Prime Minister Modi was received by the Prime Minister of Uzbekistan and the rector. He interacted with the Indologists and scholars pursuing academic interests at the Mahatma Gandhi Centre of the university. The university has an impressive record of teaching Hindi language and other Indian subjects. During his State Visit, Prime Minister announced Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language for Uzbek students. This year marks the 80th year of Hindi teaching at the university. Given the close cultural affinities between the two countries, there is admirable interest among the Uzbek students to learn Hindi. There are over 3000 words which are common between Uzbek and Hindi languages.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
4th Tri-Services Future Warfare Course concludes in New Delhi
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The fourth edition of Tri-Services Future Warfare Course, conducted under the aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and coordinated by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS), concluded on August 30, 2026 after four weeks of professional military education and deliberations at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi. The course brought together officers from the Army, Navy and Air Force, along with representatives from government organisations, academia, industry and strategic think tanks to examine emerging trends shaping the future character of warfare.

The curriculum covered geopolitical developments, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, cyber and cognitive warfare, information warfare, autonomous systems, future operations across land, maritime, air and space domains, grey-zone operations, multi-domain operations and technology-enabled warfare. The participants engaged with senior military officers, policymakers, scientists, industry leaders and subject matter experts through lectures, brainstorming sessions, scenario-building exercises, cognitive warfare simulations, field visits and participant-led presentations.

Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani interacted with the participants, seeking their views on the course and encouraging suggestions on emerging areas and additional subjects that could be incorporated in future editions to further strengthen the relevance of the programme. The course also dwelt on out-of-the-box ideas for enhancing the operational and functional efficiency of the services in an integrated ecosystem.

The valedictory programme included the presentation of certificates to the participants by the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) Air Marshal Tejinder Singh. Lt Gen SS Mahal (Retd), Managing Director Defence Research and Innovation Foundation, IIT Ropar presented 'PG Diploma in Future Warfare' to the attendees.

The fourth edition further reinforced the importance of joint learning, technological awareness, strategic foresight and operational preparedness in preparing military leaders for the evolving character of warfare. The fifth edition of the course is scheduled from November 16 till December 11, 2026.

item.description: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship MSDE in collaboration with Government of Uttar Pradesh organises PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow From Demographic Dividend to Productive Dividend: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Calls on Defence Industry to Partner with PM-SETU for a Viksit Bharat Industries must go beyond CSR and take ownership of ITIs; PM-SETU is designed to bridge the gap between skilling and employment: Jayant Chaudhary, MoS (I/C), MSDE Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE),…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MSDE in collaboration with Government of Uttar Pradesh organises PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow
From Demographic Dividend to Productive Dividend: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Calls on Defence Industry to Partner with PM-SETU for a Viksit Bharat
Industries must go beyond CSR and take ownership of ITIs; PM-SETU is designed to bridge the gap between skilling and employment: Jayant Chaudhary, MoS (I/C), MSDE
Posted On: 30 AUG 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Uttar Pradesh, today organized the PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow, bringing together senior representatives from government, industry, multilateral institutions, defence public sector enterprises, sector skill councils and skilling stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening industry participation in vocational education and transforming Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) into world-class centres of excellence.

The conclave was graced by of Minister of Defence Shri Rajnath Singh, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Deputy Chief Minister, Uttar Pradesh, Shri Brajesh Pathak and Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Kapil Dev Agarwal. Senior officials from the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Defence, Government of Uttar Pradesh and industry leaders participated in the discussions.

The event witnessed participation from senior leadership of leading defence and manufacturing organizations including Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), BrahMos Aerospace, Troop Comforts Limited (TCL), Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited (AWEIL), Gliders India Limited (GIL), Ashok Leyland, NSDC, TCIL, PTC, along with representatives from the World Bank, industry associations and other strategic stakeholders.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasized that India's journey towards becoming a global manufacturing and technology powerhouse would be driven by the availability of highly skilled manpower. He highlighted that sectors such as defence manufacturing, aerospace, electronics, drones, robotics, precision engineering and automation are witnessing rapid technological advancements and require a workforce equipped with future-ready skills. He underscored that a strong domestic defence industrial base and a strong skilling ecosystem must grow together to support India's aspirations for self-reliance and technological leadership.

The Defence Minister highlighted Uttar Pradesh's emergence as a major hub for manufacturing and defence production, driven by the rapid growth of its industrial ecosystem and the Defence Corridor. Emphasizing the importance of stronger industry-academia linkages, he noted that collaboration between industry and training institutions is crucial to equip youth with future-ready skills and expressed confidence that such partnerships would steer the state in the right direction. He further remarked that under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh is witnessing transformative development across multiple sectors.

Stressing that the availability of a skilled workforce is fundamental to nation-building, he reiterated Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of converting India's demographic dividend into a productive dividend. He underscored the need to align the skilling ecosystem with industry requirements, stating that skill certificates hold value only when they lead to meaningful employment. Calling upon industries to view PM-SETU as a collaborative mission rather than merely a government scheme, he urged them to actively participate in shaping the workforce that will ultimately serve their own growth and competitiveness.

He appealed to Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) and other defence-related organizations to actively partner in the PM-SETU initiative, while also stressing the need to transform ITIs and strengthen apprenticeship opportunities. Concluding, he stated that the success of PM-SETU should be measured not by the number of machines installed, but by the employment opportunities it creates and the lives it positively impacts.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jayant Chaudhary said that PM-SETU represents a new partnership model between government, industry and training institutions. He emphasized that the initiative is designed to bridge the gap between training and employment by enabling industries to play an active role in the development, governance and operation of ITI clusters. He highlighted that the programme aims to create a future-ready workforce through industry-aligned training, modern infrastructure, apprenticeship opportunities and pathways for entrepreneurship.

Underscoring the strategic importance of the defence sector in achieving global competitiveness, he highlighted that the industry's reliance on technology and innovation makes this scheme both timely and relevant. He called upon industries to go beyond CSR initiatives and take active ownership of ITIs to strengthen the skilling landscape.

Deputy Chief Minister Shri Brajesh Pathak assured full support to participating industries and emphasized the government's continued focus on strengthening the skilling ecosystem as a key driver towards realizing the vision of a Viksit Bharat.

Shri Kapil Dev Agrawal, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of Uttar Pradesh, said that Uttar Pradesh is committed to strengthening its skilling ecosystem to meet the needs of a rapidly expanding industrial and manufacturing base. Referring to the state's extensive network of government ITIs and the identification of eight PM-SETU clusters in Uttar Pradesh, he noted that the initiative provides a unique opportunity to align vocational training with industry requirements and emerging technologies.

Welcoming the participants, Shri Dilip Kumar, Director General -Training, highlighted the transformational potential of PM-SETU in creating a deeper and more structured engagement between industry and the skilling ecosystem. He noted that the initiative empowers Anchor Industry Partners (AIPs) to actively contribute to the growth and modernization of ITI clusters, ensuring direct alignment between institutional outcomes and industry requirements.

Dr. Hari Om, Principal Secretary, Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the significant opportunities the state offers for strengthening the skilling ecosystem and called upon industry leaders to play an active role in supporting these efforts. Smt. Manasi Sahay Thakur, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), presented an insightful overview of PM-SETU, helping the audience gain a deeper understanding of the program and its vision.

Addressing the audience, Shri Vijay Karan Anand, Chief Executive Officer, Invest UP, underscored the far-reaching benefits of the scheme and called upon officials and stakeholders to proactively participate in its rollout. He emphasized the importance of strong partnerships in realizing the scheme's vision and maximizing its impact across the state.

Representatives from defence public sector undertakings and strategic industries highlighted the growing demand for skilled technicians in areas such as aerospace systems, shipbuilding, electronics manufacturing, precision engineering, defence production, advanced welding, mechatronics and drone technologies. Industry participants reiterated their commitment to partnering with government to create sustainable talent pipelines through industry-led skilling models.

Under the PM-SETU Scheme, cluster projects comprising one Hub ITI and four Spoke ITIs can attract investments of up to ₹241 crore, supported through a funding pattern of 50% from the Government of India, 33% from State Governments and 17% from Industry Partners. Unlike traditional partnership models, the proposed Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) structure provides 51% ownership to Anchor Industry Partners, while the Centre and State Governments hold 24.5% ownership each, ensuring meaningful industry leadership in cluster development and operations. In UP so far, 32 ITIs in 8 Clusters have already been identified out of which seven are still open for collaboration.

The conclave was informed that approved Industry Partnership proposals under PM-SETU currently represent more than ₹1,500 crore of committed industry-led investment across seven clusters in five states, with several additional proposals under consideration.

During the event, NSDC and the Lucknow Cantonment Board signed an MoU to establish Shaurya Academy, a first-of-its-kind initiative aimed at preparing youth for careers in the Armed Forces, Police, and other uniformed services.
